| [9b] Sensitivity one fn | same `c_contribution()` | 0.00 |

cases.prompt_md: Rayldon Power runs a 5-site, 500MW solar fleet. A vendor offers to take over **all** O&M at a flat **$0.042M/MW** — below the fleet average of **$0.046M/MW**. Should Rayldon sign the fleet-wide deal? (Annual.)

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: (compare vendor rate to what — average or per-site marginal?)
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) at least 3 MECE buckets, and the structure tests the offer **site by site** across the 5 sites rather than on the 500MW fleet in aggregate — the $0.046M/MW figure is an average and hides dispersion; (2) states the decision rule with the right comparator: sign only where a site's own O&M cost per MW is above the vendor's $0.042M/MW, because any site already running below $0.042M/MW is made worse off by a flat fleet-wide price; (3) asks for the per-site MW split and per-site O&M cost as the first data request, before quoting any saving number.

**Fail if:** the framework prices the deal off the average — ($0.046M − $0.042M) × 500MW — or treats "the vendor is below our fleet average" as sufficient grounds to sign the fleet-wide contract; the whole case turns on the fleet-wide structure of the offer being what makes the average the wrong benchmark.

steps.label: Mental math (30–60s):
steps.candidate_md: Before the model — do it in your head. Take the vendor's price against what a megawatt costs us today: what does the deal save in a year? Thirty seconds.
steps.interviewer_md: **Expected mental estimate.** "Vendor $0.042 vs average $0.046 → saves $0.004 × 500 = $2M." The trap estimate — it uses the average.

steps.label: first-pass (decide on average).
steps.candidate_md: The vendor's flat rate against what the fleet spends on O&M today: what does the deal save Rayldon a year?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
naive_saving = 23.0 - 0.042*500   # = 2.00  -> SIGN fleet-wide
```

steps.label: Correct (#7 avg-vs-marginal).
steps.candidate_md: Three of five sites already run **below** the vendor rate. Signing fleet-wide overpays on them. Outsource only where site cost > vendor.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
correct_cost = sum((0.042*100 if om/100 > 0.042 else om) for om in [3.0,3.4,4.0,5.6,7.0])
# self-perform 1,2,3 (3.0+3.4+4.0) + outsource 4,5 (4.2+4.2) = 18.80
correct_saving = 23.0 - 18.80     # = 4.20  (more than double)
```
**Naive signs fleet-wide ($2.0M); correct outsources only the 2 degraded sites ($4.2M) — leaves $2.2M on the table.** The average masked that most sites are already cheaper than the vendor.

hints.L1: Is the decision made on the fleet average, or site by site?
hints.L2: Compare each site's own rate with the vendor rate and hand over only the sites that are worse.

steps.label: Sensitivity (which sites cross the vendor line).
steps.candidate_md: Now stress the split you just drew. Where exactly is the line here, and what would have to move for a site to change sides of it? Tell me which one goes first.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) names the **vendor $0.042** rate as the decision boundary — the per-site comparison, not the fleet average — so sites ≥$0.042/MW → outsource (**sites 4, 5**) and sites <$0.042 → self-perform (**sites 1, 2, 3**); (2) states the flip mechanism: a site changes sides when the vendor rate or that site's own O&M cost crosses that boundary, site by site; (3) works the sensitivity concretely — if the vendor rate fell to **$0.038**, site 3 at **$0.040** would also cross, giving outsource **3, 4, 5**.

**Fail if:** benchmarks against the fleet average **$0.046** instead of each site's own cost, or answers that a lower vendor rate would make the fleet-wide deal right without identifying which specific site crosses and at what rate.

steps.label: Brainstorm
steps.candidate_md: Before Rayldon signs anything with this vendor, give me at least six options that are actually on the table here — and group them for me.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups**, and the list must include: (1) renegotiate a *tiered* contract at a per-site rate (2) self-perform the good sites (3) retire or repower the worst degraded sites instead of paying premium O&M on them (4) benchmark vendor SLA against in-house uptime (5) check the per-site capacity-factor trajectory (degradation) (6) bundle only the high-cost sites into the deal

**Fail if:** the whole list is variations on sign-or-don't-sign the fleet-wide deal, with no third path beyond make-vs-buy (no retire/repower) and no per-site differentiation.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Rayldon's CEO has two minutes and wants an answer on the vendor's proposal. What do you tell him?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
*"Rayldon should reject the fleet-wide deal and outsource only Sunfield 4 and 5."* Facts: three sites already run below the vendor's $0.042/MW, so a fleet deal overpays on them; selective outsourcing saves $4.2M vs $2.0M for the fleet deal; the fleet average hid the per-site spread. Next steps: request a per-site quote for Sunfield 4–5 within 30 days; commission a degradation study to decide repower-vs-outsource on Sunfield 5.

cases.title: The Shocking Truth (Gridholm Power)
cases.header_md:
## Case 77 — The Shocking Truth (Gridholm Power) · Pricing · Medium · Trap-flip · hypothesis-update

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Utility  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap regulator reaction · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Exhibit A — Regulated economics.; table — Exhibit B — the real lever.  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 4  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① full flow-through naive ② hypothesis-update ③ **#12 regulatory clawback**

**Pricing · Utility · Medium · Trap · naive #12 regulator reaction · gen C**
*Registry: The Shocking Truth*

**Grounding (regulated electric utility).** No direct spread in project files → grounded on the **regulated-return framework**: profit is capped at *allowed ROE × rate base*, and earnings above the cap are refunded (clawback). **[DEVIATION NAMED: rate-base / allowed-return economics replace a casebook spread; the mechanic is REGULATORY CLAWBACK, not competitive response. Flag to reviewer.]**
cases.prompt_md: Gridholm Power, a regulated utility, proposes a **12% rate increase** (from $100 to $112/MWh) to lift revenue by $240M. Management projects the full $240M drops to profit. Should Gridholm expect $240M more profit? (Rate base $4,000M, allowed ROE 9%.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit A — Regulated economics.
exhibits.body_md:
**Exhibit A — Regulated economics.**

| Item | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| Rate base | $4,000M | regulated asset value |
| Allowed ROE | 9% | regulator-set |
| **Allowed profit (ceiling)** | **$360M** | 4,000 × 0.09 |
| Volume | 20,000 GWh | — |
| Current rate | $100/MWh | → revenue $2,000M |
| Opex | $1,640M | — |
| **Current profit** | **$360M** | 2,000 − 1,640 = *exactly at the allowed ceiling* |

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

exhibits.title: Exhibit B — rate-base mechanics
exhibits.body_md:
**Exhibit B — rate-base mechanics.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Allowed return applies to | rate base **as re-set at the next rate case**, including new capex |
| Grid-modernisation capex under consideration | **$1,000M** |
| Cost recovery on that capex | filed together with the rate case |

*Realised profit above the allowed return is refunded to ratepayers at the next reset.*

render_omitted.note: меньше трёх чисел, рисовать нечего

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: (does the rate hike flow to profit, or is it capped? what lifts the ceiling?)
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) names the regulatory mechanism as the binding constraint: a regulated utility earns on **rate base × allowed ROE = $4,000M × 9% = $360M**, so revenue collected above the allowed return is trued up / refunded at the next rate case — price is an input to the revenue requirement, not a lever on profit; (2) structures what **does** lift the ceiling — growing the **rate base** (approved capex additions), a higher **allowed ROE**, and cost under-run inside the test year (regulatory lag) as the only temporary way to keep upside — rather than treating the **12%** hike as the driver; (3) includes the reaction side: a rise from **$100 to $112/MWh** brings regulator and customer response (disallowance, volume/elasticity, political risk), so the **$240M** is a gross revenue number that must survive both the earnings cap and demand.

**Fail if:** the structure is revenue − cost with no allowed-return constraint, so the $240M flows to the bottom line; or the regulator appears only as an approval hurdle for the rate case, not as the mechanism that caps earnings at $360M.

steps.label: first-pass (full flow-through).
steps.candidate_md: Management says the increase drops straight to the bottom line. Run it through — what profit does Gridholm report at the new rate?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
new_revenue = 20000*1000*112/1e6      # = 2240
naive_profit = 2240 - 1640            # = 600
naive_uplift = 600 - 360              # = +240  -> "rate hike = +$240M profit"
```

steps.label: Mental math (30–60s):
steps.candidate_md: Hold on before we build anything. This is a regulated utility — take thirty seconds in your head and sanity-check the answer we just produced. Does it survive?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) computes the allowed return as 9% × $4,000M = $360M; (2) observes that Gridholm's current profit $360M already equals that allowed level, i.e. the utility is already earning its cap; (3) concludes the regulator will not let profit exceed the cap, so the naive full flow-through answer is impossible — the sign-check kills it before any model is built.

**Fail if:** the candidate accepts the $240M as dropping to profit, or moves straight into modelling the new rate without testing the current profit against the allowed 9% × $4,000M.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (before Exhibit B):
steps.candidate_md: *what happens to the extra $240M?*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Strong hypothesis: it's refunded. (Exhibit B confirms the clawback — and partly breaks the "hike is useless" conclusion: paired with capex it DOES lift profit.)

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) states the hypothesis with a direction before Exhibit B is opened — the extra **$240M** does **not** stay with Gridholm, it is clawed back / refunded to ratepayers, because profit is capped at the allowed return of **9% × $4,000M = $360M**; (2) ties it to the mechanism of rate regulation rather than to a vague "the regulator may object": the regulator resets rates so realised return returns to the allowed ROE, so the **12%** hike from **$100 to $112/MWh** earns nothing on its own; (3) names what would have to be true for the hike to pay — growth in the **rate base**, i.e. the increase paired with capex — so the hypothesis is stated in a form Exhibit B can confirm **and** partly break, not as a closed "the hike is useless".

**Fail if:** the candidate carries management's assumption that the full $240M drops to profit, or updates only to "the regulator will react somehow" without naming the clawback to the $360M ceiling — and equally if he declares the rate increase categorically pointless, missing that paired with capex it does lift profit.

steps.label: Correct (#12 regulatory clawback).
steps.candidate_md: Take the regulatory framework into account: how much of that rate increase actually reaches Gridholm's profit?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
allowed_profit = 4000*0.09            # = 360 (the ceiling)
correct_profit = min(600, 360)        # = 360
clawback = 600 - 360                  # = 240 refunded to ratepayers
correct_uplift = 360 - 360            # = 0  -> the hike ALONE earns nothing
```
**Flip: naive +$240M → correct $0** (entire uplift refunded).

hints.L1: The rate went up — does all of the increase stay with the company?
hints.L2: Hold the resulting profit against the return the regulator allows on the asset base.

steps.label: Sensitivity
steps.candidate_md: So on your own logic the hike by itself earns Gridholm nothing. What would have to be true for this to actually put money in the company's pocket — and how big would that have to be to capture the whole amount?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) identifies the only lever that moves allowed profit — the **rate base** must grow, since allowed profit = rate base × allowed ROE **9%**; the hike must therefore be *paired with capex*, not stand alone; (2) sizes a realistic case: a **$1,000M** grid-modernization program earns **+$90M**; (3) states the full-capture requirement — capturing the whole **$240M** would need **$2,667M** of new rate base, i.e. implausibly large relative to a realistic capital program.

**Fail if:** claims the $240M can be recovered through volume growth, cost cutting or a stronger filing without new invested capital; or says only "it depends on the regulator" with no rate-base arithmetic behind it.

steps.label: Brainstorm
steps.candidate_md: Step back from this particular filing — give me at least six ways a utility like Gridholm can legitimately grow profit, and group them so the list holds together.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups (regulated levers vs unregulated adjacencies)**, and the list must include: (1) rate-base growth through capex (2) an approved cost-of-capital / allowed-ROE increase (3) performance incentive mechanisms (4) non-regulated adjacent services (5) opex-efficiency sharing bands (6) decoupling riders

**Fail if:** the list is just more price-level moves (another rate increase, tariff reshuffles) with no rate-base or incentive-mechanism lever, or fails to separate what is earned inside the regulated ring-fence from what is earned outside it.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Gridholm's board is about to sign off on the rate strategy. What's your recommendation?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
*"Gridholm should not expect $240M from the rate hike — the hike alone earns $0; the profit lever is rate-base growth."* Facts: current profit already sits at the $360M allowed ceiling; a hike's excess is fully refunded via clawback; a $1,000M grid-modernization capex, paired with cost recovery, earns +$90M at the allowed 9%. Risks: (internal) capex program execution/overrun risk; (external/regulatory) the regulator may disallow part of the capex from rate base. Next steps: file a rate case pairing the capex with cost recovery within the next cycle; model the allowed-return sensitivity to a possible ROE cut.

**Six-check table (#77).**

| Check | Result | Discrepancy |
|---|---|---|
| Derive-first | all exhibit rows from rate base × ROE | allowed profit 360 = 4000×0.09 |
| [1] Rounding chain | round once | 0.00 |
| [6] Metric unity | `profit_uplift()` one function, both levers | ✓ |
| [9b] Sensitivity one fn | same function, args only | 0.00 |
| Flip integrity | naive 240 → correct 0 (clawback) | direction flip real |
| Interaction check | capex-only AND hike-only both = 0; both together = 90 | verified logic |

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Gridholm should not expect $240M from the rate hike — the hike alone earns $0; the profit lever is rate-base growth."* Facts: current profit already sits at the $360M allowed ceiling; a hike's excess is fully refunded via clawback; a $1,000M grid-modernization capex, paired with cost recovery, earns +$90M at the allowed 9%. ## Case 78 — The Grand Budapest Hotel (Staymore Hotels) · Pricing · **Easy** · Trap-flip

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Hotels  
> **Difficulty:🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap expected value · **Время:** —

> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 4  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① overbook = no-show rate (naive) ② **#11 expected value**, walk cost — суть

**Pricing · Hotels · Easy · Trap · naive #11 expected value · gen C**
*Registry: The Grand Budapest Hotel*

**Setting:** Central/Eastern Europe; Staymore's **Budapest flagship** (300 rooms). *(Title dictates setting — a "Grand Budapest Hotel" case is set in Budapest, not Miami.)*

**Grounding (Kellogg Hospitality Co p.13):** rooms × occupancy × days; fixed + variable cost per night; business-traveler clientele; the room-night is *perishable inventory*.
cases.prompt_md: Staymore's Budapest flagship runs an 8% no-show rate. Revenue management proposes **overbooking by 8% (24 rooms)** to offset no-shows and capture ~$4,320/night in otherwise-lost revenue. Is that the right overbooking level?

exhibits.title: Exhibit A — No-show distribution (nightly).
exhibits.body_md:
**Exhibit A — No-show distribution (nightly).**

| No-shows | 15 | 20 | 24 | 28 | 33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.15 | 0.25 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 0.10 |

Expected no-shows ≈ **23** (~8% of 300).

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Overbooking parameters
exhibits.body_md:
| Parameter | Unit | Value |

| ADR | $/room-night | $180 |
| Cost of walking a guest | $/guest | $2,200 |

*Walking a guest costs the competitor's premium rate, upgrade compensation and loyalty damage.*

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd decide whether that's the right level.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) frames overbooking as an expected-value tradeoff rather than a rule that the overbooking level should match the no-show rate; (2) names the upside explicitly — an extra room sold at ADR $180, only in the states of the world where the booked guest does not show; (3) names the downside explicitly — walking a guest at $2,200, incurred whenever more guests show than there are rooms; (4) states that the right level is where marginal expected revenue equals marginal expected walk cost, and flags the asymmetry between $180 and $2,200.

**Fail if:** the structure sets overbooking equal to the 8% no-show rate (24 rooms) as “free money”, or omits the walk-cost side entirely, or treats the no-show rate as a certainty rather than a distribution.

steps.label: first-pass (overbook = no-show rate).
steps.candidate_md: Start with revenue management's logic: at an 8% no-show rate, how many rooms is that and what does it add per night?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
naive_overbook = 300*0.08          # = 24 rooms
naive_revenue  = 24*180            # = $4,320/night  "free money" (assumes exactly 8% no-show)
```

steps.label: Mental math (30–60s):
steps.candidate_md: Take thirty seconds and pressure-test revenue management's plan out loud — is that $4,320 really free money? Think about what a single night can actually look like.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) states that the **8%** no-show rate is an *average* and that actual no-shows vary night to night — some nights only **15**; (2) quantifies the downside on such a night: overbooking **24** against **15** no-shows means walking **9** guests at **$2,200** = **$19,800** hit; (3) draws the conclusion that this single-night loss dwarfs the $4,320 upside, so the point estimate is a trap and the overbooking level must be set off the distribution of outcomes, not the mean.

**Fail if:** treats the 8% as certain and confirms 24 rooms / $4,320 as free money; or mentions that no-shows "vary" qualitatively without pricing out one bad night in walk cost.

steps.label: Correct (#11 expected value).
steps.candidate_md: Run the numbers across the demand scenarios in the exhibit and tell me what overbooking level Staymore should set, with the value at that level.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
scenarios = {15:0.15, 20:0.25, 24:0.30, 28:0.20, 33:0.10}
def ev(N):   # overbook N rooms
    return sum(p*(min(N,s)*180 - max(0,N-s)*2200) for s,p in scenarios.items())
# EV(15)=+2700 | EV(20)=+1815 | EV(24)=−1273 (LOSS) | EV(28)=−7217
# optimal overbook = 15 rooms (EV +$2,700/night)
```
**Flip: naive "overbook 24 = +$4,320 free" → correct "24 LOSES $1,273/night; optimal is 15."** The naive level ignores walk cost entirely; at 24 rooms the high-show scenarios turn it negative.

hints.L1: Are you working one demand scenario, or the expected value across all of them?
hints.L2: Compute the expected result at each overbooking level and take the maximum, not the average scenario.

steps.label: Sensitivity (walk cost is the crux).
steps.candidate_md: Walk cost is the number I'd least trust. Rerun the optimal overbooking level at $900, $1,500 and $2,200 per walked guest — what's the pattern, and what does it do to the proposal on the table?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# walk $900 -> optimal 20 | walk $1,500 -> optimal 15 | walk $2,200 -> optimal 15, naive-24 negative
```
Higher walk cost → lower optimal overbook. Annual (350 nights): optimal +$0.945M vs naive −$0.446M.

steps.label: Brainstorm
steps.candidate_md: Whatever we land on for the booking policy, Staymore still has a no-show problem. Give me at least six levers management has here, and group them for me.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups (reduce-no-shows vs manage-the-walk-risk)**, and the list must include: (1) tiered deposit/prepay to cut no-shows (2) waitlist/standby fill (3) dynamic walk-cost partnerships with nearby hotels (4) a no-show fee (5) corporate-contract guaranteed rooms (6) same-day discount to fill

**Fail if:** every idea is a tweak to the overbooking number itself, with nothing that attacks the no-show rate at source and nothing that lowers the cost of a walk.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: The revenue-management head is waiting on your answer for how Staymore should handle its bookings. Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
*"Staymore should overbook by 15 rooms, not 24."* Facts: at $2,200 walk cost, overbooking 24 loses $1,273/night because no-shows vary below 24 on ~40% of nights; 15 rooms maximizes EV at +$2,700/night; the naive "$4,320 free" ignores walk cost entirely. Risks: (internal) walk events damage loyalty beyond the modeled cost; (external) a competitor's rate spike raises the walk cost and lowers the optimal further. Next steps: implement 15-room overbooking with a real-time walk-cost feed; pilot prepay deposits to cut the no-show rate itself.

## Case 79 — Between a Rock and a Hard Place (Quarrix Materials) · Market Entry · Medium · **Clean**

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** Aggregates  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Clean · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Exhibit A — Entry economics (all derived).  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① clean-проверки (есть ли скрытая freight-ловушка) ② **CLEAN**: correct=naive=ENTER ③ sensitivity «что БЫ перевернуло» — freight breakeven $5/т

**Market Entry · Aggregates · Medium · Clean · gen C**
*Registry: Between a Rock and a Hard Place*

**Grounding (Stern Industrials p.22):** capacity utilization; aggregates are heavy/low-value → economically freight-bound (~50-mile radius). **[DEVIATION NAMED: aggregates ≈ Industrials, but FREIGHT RADIUS replaces book-to-bill as the market-capping metric. Flag to reviewer.]**

**Clean-case purpose.** A trap-trained candidate will *hunt* for a freight/capacity death-trap (a #6 capacity reversal) and want to reject entry. Correct: the freight radius genuinely limits the market, but the economics still clear the hurdle → **ENTER**. Validate that no hidden capacity/freight killer exists.
cases.prompt_md: Quarrix Materials (aggregates) considers entering a new metro by building a quarry+plant. Demand is 5,000 kt/yr; Quarrix can win ~60%. Should it enter? (WACC 10%; the quarry runs indefinitely — value it as a perpetuity.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit A — Entry economics (all derived).
exhibits.body_md:
**Exhibit A — Entry economics (all derived).**

| Item | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| Metro demand | 5,000 kt/yr | — |
| Winnable @60% | 3,000 kt | 5,000 × 0.60 |
| Plant capacity | 3,500 kt | > winnable → not binding |
| Volume served | 3,000 kt | min(3,000, 3,500) |
| Contribution/ton | $5 | 14 − 7 − 2 |
| Annual contribution | $15M | 3,000 kt × $5/ton |
| Fixed | $3M | — |
| **Annual profit** | **$12M** | 15 − 3 |

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Entry parameters
exhibits.body_md:
| Parameter | Unit | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $/ton | $14 |
| Production cost | $/ton | $7 |
| Freight | $/ton | $2 |
| Capex | $ | $30M |
| Plant capacity | kt/yr | 3,500 kt |
| Fixed cost | $/yr | $3M |
| WACC | % | 10% |

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and structure how you'd approach the decision.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) sizes the market Quarrix can actually serve rather than the headline 5,000 kt — aggregates are freight-bound, so the reachable demand is limited by haul economics, then ≈60% share; (2) checks whether plant capacity of 3,500 kt binds the volume the share implies; (3) builds unit economics as $14 − $7 − $2 = $5 per ton contribution, less $3M/yr fixed, and values the stream as a perpetuity at WACC 10%; (4) compares that value against the $30M capex to reach an enter/don't-enter answer.

**Fail if:** the candidate treats all 5,000 kt as addressable, skips the capacity check, or builds a revenue/cost tree that never reaches an NPV-vs-capex comparison.

steps.label: Mental math (30–60s):
steps.candidate_md: Before we get precise — run the rough economics in your head. Is this even in the ballpark of being worth building? Thirty seconds.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) sizes winnable volume as ~60% of 5,000 kt = **3,000 kt** and per-ton contribution net of freight ($14 − $7 − $2 = **$5**), giving **3,000 kt × $5 = $15M** contribution; (2) nets the fixed cost and capitalizes: less **$3M** fixed = **$12M/yr** → perpetuity **$120M** against the **$30M** capex; (3) labels the answer as provisional — clearly positive *unless something caps it* — and names that he will now hunt for the cap (plant capacity bind, freight reach, competitive response) rather than closing on the estimate.

**Fail if:** multiplies price by volume without subtracting freight (or forgets the $3M fixed), or declares "enter" as a settled answer off the back-of-envelope with no constraint check queued.

steps.label: The clean checks (is there a hidden freight/capacity killer?).
steps.candidate_md: Before we land on a number, check whether plant capacity or freight breaks this. Then give me the NPV of entering.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# capacity: winnable 3,000 kt < plant capacity 3,500 kt -> NOT binding, no lost upside
# freight: $2/ton leaves contribution $5/ton POSITIVE -> no margin kill
# NPV = 12/0.10 - 30 = +90  -> ENTER
```

steps.label: Correct = first-pass = ENTER.
steps.candidate_md: Now bring the freight radius and the plant's capacity into the model. Redo the value of entering — where does it land?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
npv = 12/0.10 - 30    # = +90   (both paths agree)
```
No reversal to invent. The freight radius is real but does not bite at these economics.

hints.L1: Is the demand you took physically reachable from this plant?
hints.L2: Check the volume against the plant's capacity and the freight radius before valuing entry.

steps.label: Sensitivity (what WOULD flip it — clean confirmation).
steps.candidate_md: How sensitive is the entry decision to freight cost and to the share Quarrix wins? Tell me where each one flips the answer.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def npv79(share, freight=2, capex=30):
    vol = min(5000*share, 3500)
    return (vol*(14-7-freight)/1000 - 3)/0.10 - capex
# freight breakeven = $5.00/ton (above this, contribution too thin -> entry flips to NO)
# breakeven share ~ 0.24 (base 0.60 is 150% above)
```
Entry survives up to $5/ton freight (base $2) — robustly positive. The candidate confirms the feared freight/capacity trap does not materialize.

---

### 🔍 Гипотезы разворота (перечень обязателен для Clean)

**Гипотеза 1 — конечный срок жизни карьера вместо бессрочности.** Предполагаем, что запасы исчерпываются через несколько лет:
```
30 / 12 = 2.50
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: нужный аннуитетный фактор 2.50 лежит между тремя и четырьмя годами по ставке 10%, то есть карьеру достаточно прожить чуть больше трёх лет — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 2 — ставка дисконтирования.** Предполагаем стоимость капитала выше напечатанной:
```
12 / 30 = 0.40
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: ставку надо учетверить, до 40%, чтобы вход перестал окупаться — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 3 — потолок мощности завода.** Предполагаем, что вся доступная доля рынка берётся и объём упирается в мощность:
```
3,500 × 5 / 1000 = 17.5
17.5 − 3 = 14.5
14.5 / 0.10 − 30 = 115
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: ограничение объёма сверху лишь увеличивает результат — до 115 против 90 — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза «все проверенные стрессы ОДНОВРЕМЕННО».** Обе величины из предыдущих гипотез — это ПОРОГИ, а не сценарии; складывать порог с порогом нельзя. Считаем то, что складывать можно: совместное условие входа.
```
NPV ≥ 0  ⟺  доля × (7 − фрахт) ≥ 1.20
сегодня: 0.60 × (7 − 2) = 3.00 — запас 2.50×
обнуление при одновременном движении обоих рычагов: t = 61.3% пути к их порогам
на трети пути: NPV = $36,000,000
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: базовый NPV $90,000,000 держится, но настоящий запас — 2.50× по ПРОИЗВЕДЕНИЮ, а не 150% по доле, как сказано в кейсе по одному рычагу. Разворот наступает, когда оба рычага пройдут 61.3% пути к своим порогам одновременно.

*Метод: вводим единую долю t — все рычаги одновременно проходят долю t пути от фактического значения до СВОЕГО порога. при t = 100% все рычаги стоят на своих порогах одновременно. Запас по одному рычагу — не запас.*

steps.label: Framework + open-drive.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd approach this. Then tell me where you want to start — rider demand, driver supply, per-trip unit economics, or incumbent presence — and why.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) structure treats this as a two-sided marketplace — rider demand, driver supply, unit economics and competition all present, with a cost side, not a demand-only tree; (2) states a hypothesis before choosing a direction; (3) opens on driver supply/liquidity as the binding concern — holding the sub-10-minute pickup SLA requires ~150 drivers on-call at a guaranteed $2,500/month regardless of trips — then moves to per-trip unit economics (take rate 25% on $45); (4) keeps the $4M entry cost and WACC 10% in view as the hurdle the annual profit must clear.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (before the driver exhibit):
steps.candidate_md: *what will driver economics show?*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Strong hypothesis: a liquidity floor cost will erode profit. (The exhibit partly confirms the concern is worth checking — and breaks it: the floor doesn't actually bite at this volume.)

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) states a directional, falsifiable hypothesis before the exhibit: the **$2,500/month** guarantee across the ~**150** on-call drivers is a fixed liquidity floor required by the <10-min-pickup SLA, and it erodes take-rate profit whenever demand per driver is thin; (2) names the quantity that tests it: monthly trips per driver = **5,000** riders × **3** trips = **15,000** trips ÷ **150** drivers = **100** trips/driver, and compares what a driver earns on that volume against the **$2,500** floor — the cost to Ridemos is the top-up, max(0, guarantee − driver earnings), not the guarantee itself; (3) says in advance what each outcome implies: if driver earnings clear $2,500 the floor costs nothing and the entry case stands on the **25%** take rate against the **$4M** entry cost; if they fall short, Ridemos pays the shortfall on every driver every month.

**Fail if:** the candidate offers no hypothesis and simply asks to see driver data, or treats the guarantee as an unconditional cost of $2,500 × 150 per month regardless of what drivers earn from trips.

steps.label: The clean check (does the liquidity floor bite?).
steps.candidate_md: Look at the driver side: at that demand and that driver count, what does a driver make in a month, and how much do we have to top up to meet the guarantee?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
trips_per_driver = 15000/150            # = 100/month
driver_earnings  = 100 * 45 * 0.75      # = $3,375/month (drivers keep 75% of fare)
guarantee        = 2500
topup = max(0, guarantee - driver_earnings)   # = max(0, 2500-3375) = $0
# drivers self-sustain on trip earnings -> NO liquidity subsidy needed -> feared floor doesn't bite
```

steps.label: Correct = first-pass = ENTER.
steps.candidate_md: Give me the economics of entering this city — annual profit and the value against the entry cost. Do we go in?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
profit = 2.03 - 1.20        # = 0.83
npv = 0.83/0.10 - 4         # = +4.25   (106% over the $4M entry cost)
```
No reversal to invent. The liquidity concern is real to *check* but does not materialize.

hints.L1: Look at what the company owes the driver regardless of how many trips come in.
hints.L2: State which year's economics the perpetuity assumes before dividing by the discount rate.

steps.label: Sensitivity (when WOULD the floor bite — clean confirmation).
steps.candidate_md: Demand is the assumption I'd challenge. At how few premium riders does the driver guarantee start costing us money, and at how few does entry stop making sense? Keep those two thresholds separate.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# TWO distinct thresholds (keep them separate):
#  (1) topup STARTS: driver earnings = guarantee -> trips/driver = 2500/(45*0.75) = 74.07
#      -> riders = 74.07 * 150 / 3 = 3,704 riders. Below this, the subsidy kicks in.
#  (2) DECISION reverses (NPV=0): at ~3,951 riders — and this happens BEFORE the floor
#      starts to bite at 3,704. Between 3,704 and 3,951 the top-up is still $0 and the
#      bites but entry is still NPV-positive; only below ~3,951 does entry flip to NO.
# base 5,000 riders > both thresholds -> robust ENTER
```
At 3,000 riders NPV is negative (subsidy dominates); at 3,704 the topup just begins; at ~3,951 NPV crosses zero; at 4,000+ NPV is positive and topup is $0. Base 5,000 clears both thresholds comfortably. **Note the ~25% margin to reversal (5,000 vs 3,951) — this is a more borderline clean than #79's freight margin (150%).**

---

### 🔍 Гипотезы разворота (перечень обязателен для Clean)

**Гипотеза 1 — число водителей, требуемых уровнем сервиса.** Предполагаем, что для обещанной подачи нужно больше водителей, и гарантия начинает стоить денег:
```
15,000 × 33.75 / 2,500 = 202.5
6,500,000 / 30,000 = 216.7
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: база 150 водителей лежит на 26% ниже порога включения субсидии и на 31% ниже порога разворота — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 2 — тариф не удержится на премиальном уровне.** Предполагаем падение цены поездки:
```
1,600,000 / 45,000 = 35.56
2,500 / (100 × 0.75) = 33.33
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: тариф должен упасть на 21%, до $35.56, и разворот наступает раньше, чем включается гарантия — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 3 — конечный горизонт вместо бессрочности.** Предполагаем, что город приносит поток не вечно:
```
4 / 0.825 = 4.848
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: нужный аннуитетный фактор 4.848 достигается на седьмом году по ставке 10%, а промпт задаёт бессрочную конвенцию — вывод **не переворачивается**; это самый узкий запас кейса.

**Гипотеза «все проверенные стрессы ОДНОВРЕМЕННО».** Спрос и тариф падают вместе. Оба входят в результат только произведением, поэтому считаем его:
```
NPV ≥ 0  ⟺  райдеры × тариф ≥ 177,778
сегодня: 5,000 × $45 = 225,000 — запас 26.6%
обнуление при одновременном движении: t = 53.0%
на трети пути: NPV = $1,516,876
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: NPV $4,250,000 держится, а доплата по гарантии включается позже разворота и знака не решает. Но запас — 26.6% по произведению, и это тоньше, чем выглядит каждый рычаг по отдельности.

*Метод: вводим единую долю t — все рычаги одновременно проходят долю t пути от фактического значения до СВОЕГО порога. при t = 100% все рычаги стоят на своих порогах одновременно. Запас по одному рычагу — не запас.*

steps.label: Brainstorm
steps.candidate_md: Before Ridemos commits a dollar to this market, what would you want confirmed first? Give me six, and group them so I can see the logic behind the list.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — and the list must be a *confirm-liquidity checklist*, not generic market entry.

**Pass if ALL:** (1) at least six distinct checks, organized into at least two candidate-named buckets; (2) the supply/driver side is covered — that ~**150** drivers can be recruited without extra subsidy, the incumbent's driver lock-in, surge-hour coverage gaps, and whether the **<10-min** pickup SLA is genuinely achievable with 150 drivers spread across the coverage zones; (3) the demand and access side is covered — stress-testing the **3 trips/month** per-rider frequency, and confirming airport permit/access.

**Fail if:** fewer than six ideas, an ungrouped flat list, or generic entry checks (competitor reaction, marketing budget, brand awareness) with no link to driver liquidity, the guarantee, or the SLA.

cases.title: Fight Club (Reptrix)
cases.header_md:
## Case 81 — Fight Club (Reptrix) · Pricing · **Medium** · Trap-flip · hypothesis-update

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Fitness  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap cannibalization · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Exhibit — Catchment study.  
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 4  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① naive revenue ② hypothesis-update ③ каннибализация

**Pricing · Fitness · Medium · Trap · naive #10 cannibalization · gen C**
*Registry: Fight Club*

**Pricing · Fitness · F1 · Ловушка #10 (cannibalization)**
*Grounding: Retail p.13 recurring-traffic — [DEVIATION NAMED: membership subscription + catchment cannibalization замещает in-store footfall].*
cases.prompt_md: Reptrix, a fitness-club chain, wants to open a **new club** in a growing district, 2 miles from an existing Reptrix club. The new site projects **3,000 members** at **$40/month**. Fixed cost of the new club is **$0.9M/yr**. Should Reptrix open it? (WACC 10%, perpetuity.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Catchment study.
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Catchment study.** Of the 3,000 projected members, **45% are transfers** from the existing Reptrix club 2 miles away (same catchment). The existing club loses those members' revenue.

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

steps.label: Framework (open-drive-lite).
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute, and then walk me through how you'd approach this decision.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) states a hypothesis first, then lays out at least three MECE buckets, with both incremental revenue and incremental cost of the new club explicitly on the page (2) puts the existing Reptrix club 2 miles away into the structure — an explicit bucket or test of whether the 3,000 projected members are *truly new* to the chain, i.e. catchment overlap between the two clubs (3) closes by handing the structure back — "does that work for you?"

**Fail if:** the candidate treats all 3,000 members as incremental to Reptrix without ever questioning the nearby club, or builds a revenue-and-cost structure that only ever looks at the new site in isolation.

steps.label: first-pass revenue.
steps.candidate_md: What does the new club bring in over a year on those members and that fee, net of its fixed cost — and what's that worth at a 10% discount rate?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
WACC=D('0.10')
new_members=D('3000'); annual_fee=D('40')*12   # $480/yr
gross_rev=new_members*annual_fee/D('1000000')  # $1.44M
fixed=D('0.9')
naive_profit=gross_rev-fixed                   # 0.54
naive_value=naive_profit/WACC                  # 5.4
```
Naive: gross revenue **$1.44M/yr**, minus fixed **$0.9M** = **$0.54M/yr** → value **$5.4M** → looks like a clear OPEN.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: 3,000 × $480 ≈ 3,000 × $500 = $1.5M gross; minus ~$0.9M ≈ $0.6M/yr. Positive at first glance — *"прикинь устно, точный расчёт — после"*.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) does the round-number arithmetic and states the rounding direction: 3,000 × **$480** approximated as 3,000 × **$500** = **$1.5M** gross, less the **$0.9M** fixed cost ≈ **$0.6M**/yr, with the note that $500-for-$480 overstates it (exact: $1.44M gross, $0.54M net); (2) capitalizes at the **10%** WACC — ≈**$6M** on the round number, ≈**$5.4M** exact — and states the sign: positive on first pass; (3) labels the number as **gross, not incremental** — the new site is **2 miles** from an existing Reptrix club, so some of the **3,000** members are transfers, and the estimate is an upper bound until catchment data arrives.

**Fail if:** ≈$0.6M/yr and ≈$6M are presented as the answer to "should Reptrix open it", with no statement that revenue at the existing club is untouched in this arithmetic; or the candidate declines to estimate and asks for exact numbers instead of doing the mental check.
steps.candidate_md_en: 3,000 × $480 ≈ 3,000 × $500 = $1.5M gross; minus ~$0.9M ≈ $0.6M/yr. Positive at first glance — *"estimate it in your head, the exact calculation comes after"*.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Before we look at the catchment data — what share of the 3,000 do you expect are genuinely new vs. poached from the nearby club?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Strong hypothesis: meaningful overlap given 2-mile distance. Weak: assume all new.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) the candidate commits to a share **before** the catchment data — a meaningful minority (not a token share, and not all) of the **3,000** projected members are expected to be transfers from the existing Reptrix club — and states that range out loud rather than saying "we'd need the data"; (2) the mechanism for overlap is named and tied to the **2 miles**: catchment circles at that distance largely overlap, and existing members will trade across to the newer club, so the driver is distance and site substitutability, not marketing; (3) the candidate states why a transferred member is worth zero incrementally — Reptrix already books that **$40/month** (**$480/yr**) — so those members inflate revenue at the new club while adding none to the chain; (4) the consequence for the step-3 estimate is stated: the **~$0.6M/yr** surplus (**$1.5M** gross less **$0.9M** fixed) is an overstatement that shrinks roughly in proportion to the transfer share, so the first-glance positive is not safe.

**Fail if:** the candidate assumes all **3,000** are genuinely new, or gives no directional call at all; also fail if cannibalisation is framed only as a brand or member-experience issue (crowding, cannibalising the old club's atmosphere) rather than as revenue Reptrix already earns being double-counted in the new club's projection.

steps.label: Correct (cannibalization).
steps.candidate_md: How many of the 3,000 members at the new club are genuinely new to Reptrix? Rework the annual economics on that basis and give me your answer.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
transfer_share=D('0.45')
transfers=new_members*transfer_share           # 1350
lost_rev=transfers*annual_fee/D('1000000')     # 0.648  (revenue already ours)
true_incremental_rev=gross_rev-lost_rev        # 0.792
correct_profit=true_incremental_rev-fixed      # -0.108
correct_value=correct_profit/WACC              # -1.08
```
Correct: only **55% (1,650 members)** are truly new. True incremental revenue = **$0.792M**, minus fixed **$0.9M** = **−$0.108M/yr** → value **−$1.08M** → **DO NOT OPEN**.

hints.L1: Чем новый клуб отличается от того, что уже стоит рядом?
hints.L2: Спроси, какая доля будущих участников уже ходит в наш соседний клуб.

hints_en.L1: How is the new club different from the one already standing next door?
hints_en.L2: Ask what share of the future members already go to our club nearby.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: How much of the new club's membership can come from the existing club before opening stops making sense? Show me the value either side of that point.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def value_at(share):
    lost=new_members*share*annual_fee/D('1000000')
    return ((gross_rev-lost)-fixed)/WACC
# breakeven transfer share:
breakeven = 1 - fixed/gross_rev                 # 0.375
```
Breakeven transfer share = **37.5%**. Below that the club adds value; the actual 45% puts it underwater. At 30% transfers value would be **+$1.08M** (open); at 50%, **−$1.8M**.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Given what we just found, suppose Reptrix still wants a club in that district. Give me at least six ways they could make this work — and group them.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — book list: differentiate the format (24/7 vs classes), reprice to expand the pie, target a non-overlapping micro-segment, relocate 0.5mi further out, convert the old club's freed capacity to premium PT, cross-sell both sites as one membership, close the older site and consolidate.

**Fail if:** fewer than 6 ideas, no grouping, or every idea is a marketing push to add members without addressing the fact that the two catchments overlap — the candidate must include at least one option acting on the *existing* club (freed capacity, consolidation, cross-sell).

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Reptrix's CEO asks: do we open the new club or not? Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Что общего у нового клуба со старым в 2 милях?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal catchment study: 45% are transfers.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Catchment study:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "catchment overlap" · "are members new" · "transfers from existing club" · "cannibalization" · "distance to nearest club".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Catchment study', 'triggers': ['catchment overlap', 'are members new', 'transfers from existing club', 'cannibalization', 'distance to nearest club']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Reptrix should NOT open the new club as scoped — it destroys ~$1.1M of value because 45% of projected members merely transfer from an existing club 2 miles away."* Facts: gross $1.44M but true incremental only $0.79M < $0.9M fixed; breakeven overlap is 37.5% and actual is 45%. Risks: (internal) transfer estimate is soft — a survey could revise it; (external) a competitor could open in the district if Reptrix doesn't, capturing the genuinely-new 55%. Next steps: run a member-address survey to firm the 45%; test a differentiated format that expands total catchment before committing capex.

> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask whether the two clubs' catchments overlap / whether memb

cases.header_md:
## Case 82 — Showtime Lakers (Backcourt Athletic) · Profitability · **Medium** · Trap-flip · open-drive

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Basketball  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap gross-vs-net · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (1):** waterfall — Exhibit — Revenue-share waterfall.  
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① gross naive ② open-drive reveal ③ **net waterfall — вывести каждый слой**

**Profitability · Basketball · Medium · Trap · naive #4 gross-vs-net · gen C**
*Registry: Showtime Lakers*

**Profitability · Pro basketball franchise · F2 · Ловушка #4 (gross-vs-net)**
*Setting: Minneapolis (the franchise's home — title dictates geography). Grounding: Media p.20 audience monetization — [DEVIATION NAMED: live-event gate + arena revenue-share waterfall замещает ad-ARPU].*
cases.prompt_md: Backcourt Athletic, a Minneapolis pro-basketball franchise, is weighing a **premium courtside expansion** projected to add **$320,000 of gross arena revenue per home game** (41 home games). The build is financed at **$9M/yr**. Management says it clearly pays. Does it? (Consider how arena revenue is shared.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Revenue-share waterfall.
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Revenue-share waterfall.** Incremental arena revenue splits: **ticket portion 60%, concession portion 40%**. The **arena owner takes 30%** of all arena revenue; the **league gate-share pool takes 6%** of the ticket portion; the **visiting team takes 10%** of the incremental ticket portion.

steps.label: Framework + open-drive.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd test whether this expansion actually pays. Then tell me where you want to start — I can give you the gross incremental revenue, the arena lease and revenue-share terms, the league gate-sharing rules, or the financing cost. Your call on the order.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) structures the test as *incremental profit to the franchise* against the **$9M/yr** financing — i.e. explicitly flags that the **$320,000 per game** is a gross arena figure and not yet the franchise's money; (2) chooses to pull the revenue-share terms first — the **arena lease / revenue-share terms (b)** and the **league gate-sharing rules (c)** — before trusting the gross line, and says why: those two determine the share retained; (3) leaves the **financing cost (d)** and the **gross revenue (a)** as confirmatory inputs rather than starting points.

**Fail if (red flag):** computes $320,000 × 41 games and puts it straight against the $9M financing to declare it pays; or opens on gross revenue or financing cost and treats revenue sharing as a detail to check later.

steps.label: first-pass (gross).
steps.candidate_md: Take management's case at face value: what does the courtside expansion add to annual profit once financing is paid?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
games=D('41'); gross_pg=D('320000'); fin=D('9')
gross_annual=gross_pg*games/D('1000000')       # 13.12
naive_profit=gross_annual-fin                   # 4.12
```
Naive: $320k × 41 = **$13.12M/yr** gross, minus $9M financing = **+$4.12M** → approve.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update / open-drive reveal.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Does the franchise keep all $320k per game?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
The franchise does **not** own 100% of arena revenue — there is a share waterfall.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) Explicitly drops the gross figure: the **$320,000 per game** is *arena* revenue, not franchise revenue, so the annual number built from it over **41 home games** cannot be compared with the **$9M/yr** financing. (2) Names at least two distinct claimants standing between that gross and the franchise's own P&L — e.g. the arena operator's share, league-wide revenue sharing, and the visiting-team share — rather than gesturing at "other costs." (3) Turns the hypothesis into a data request: asks for the share percentage at each level of the waterfall (and which revenue line each is applied to) so the per-game gross can be walked down to net, and states that only that net figure is comparable with the $9M/yr financing.

**Fail if:** Candidate stays on $320,000 × 41 games and concludes the expansion clearly pays; or reframes the gap as an operating-cost question (staffing, F&B, maintenance) instead of a revenue-share waterfall; or acknowledges that revenue is shared but never asks for the percentages needed to net it down.

steps.label: Correct (net waterfall, derive each layer).
steps.candidate_md: Take the projected gross revenue per game through to what lands in the franchise's own P&L, scale it to a full season and compare it with the financing. Does the expansion pay?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
arena_cut=D('0.30'); league=D('0.06'); visitor=D('0.10')
ticket=gross_pg*D('0.60')                        # 192000
after_arena=gross_pg*(1-arena_cut)               # 224000
league_take=ticket*league                        # 11520
visitor_take=ticket*visitor                      # 19200
net_pg=after_arena-league_take-visitor_take      # 193280
net_annual=net_pg*games/D('1000000')             # 7.924
correct_profit=net_annual-fin                    # -1.076
```
Correct: after the waterfall the franchise keeps **$193,280/game** → **$7.92M/yr** net, minus $9M = **−$1.08M** → **REJECT**.

hints.L1: Does the team keep all of the arena's revenue?
hints.L2: Ask how the gate is split before treating the ticket price as revenue to the team.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Before we walk the numbers through properly, give me a thirty-second mental check: does this expansion cover its financing, and how close is it?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) recognizes the franchise keeps only ~60% of gross after all shares — roughly $193k of the $320k per game (2) scales it: $193k × 41 ≈ $7.9M for the season (3) compares to the $9M/yr financing and calls it negative, stated as a flag *before* the full model confirms it

**Fail if:** multiplies the $320,000 gross by 41 games, compares that to $9M, and concludes the project clearly pays.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: How much gross revenue per home game would this expansion actually need to cover the financing? Tell me how that compares with what management has projected.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def net_profit(gpg):
    t=gpg*D('0.60'); net=gpg*D('0.70')-t*D('0.06')-t*D('0.10')
    return net*games/D('1000000')-fin
# breakeven gross/game where net covers $9M:
```
The project needs roughly **$363k gross/game** (not $320k) for the net to cover $9M — a **13% higher** gate than projected. The gross-vs-net gap ($13.12M vs $7.92M) is the whole story.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Say ownership still wants to go ahead with the courtside build. Give me at least six ways to improve the economics of this project, grouped.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — book list: renegotiate the arena split at lease renewal, shift the mix toward concessions (only the arena cut applies, no league or visitor take), add non-gate premium such as sponsorship suites outside the share pool, stagger the build to cut financing, bundle season-ticket premiums, monetize the space on non-game days.

**Fail if:** fewer than 6 ideas, no grouping, or every idea raises gross revenue per game without touching what the franchise actually keeps — at least one idea must move revenue outside the share pool or change the split itself.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: The ownership group is in the room — approve the courtside expansion or not? What do you recommend?
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Команда оставляет весь доход с арены себе?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal waterfall: arena 30% / league 6% gate / visitor 10% ticket.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Revenue-share waterfall:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "revenue share" · "arena lease terms" · "league gate sharing" · "who owns arena revenue" · "net vs gross".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Revenue-share waterfall', 'triggers': ['revenue share', 'arena lease terms', 'league gate sharing', 'who owns arena revenue', 'net vs gross']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Backcourt should NOT approve the courtside expansion as structured — the revenue-share waterfall leaves only $7.9M net against $9M financing, a $1.1M annual loss."* Facts: gross $13.12M is misleading; after arena 30% + league 6% + visitor 10% the team nets $193k/game; breakeven needs 13% more gross. Risks: (internal) financing terms may be renegotiable, changing the verdict; (external/regulatory) league gate-sharing rules can change and further cut the net. Next steps: model a concession-weighted design (avoids league/visitor take); reopen the arena split before committing.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask how arena revenue is split / whether the team owns 100% of it.

cases.single_carrier_reason: носитель один по замыслу: вся числовая часть кейса — один связный объект (memo / таблица / график), и разрезать его на два экзибита можно только выдумав данные, чего цех не делает
cases.difficulty_test: Доход с арены делится по регламенту лиги и договору с гостевой командой: до клуба доходит не то, что напечатано на билете.

cases.title: The Pimpsons (Vireno Media)
cases.header_md:
## Case 83 — The Pimpsons (Vireno Media) · Growth Strategy · **Medium** · Trap-flip · hypothesis-update

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Growth Strategy · **Индустрия:** Streaming  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap realized-vs-lifetime · **Время:** Streaming  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Exhibit — Retention.  
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① realized year-1 ② hypothesis-update ③ **lifetime, полная многолетняя цепочка [4]** + F6

**Growth Strategy · Streaming · Medium · Trap · naive #5 realized-vs-lifetime · gen C**
*Registry: The Pimpsons*

**Growth Strategy · TV/streaming · F6 · Ловушка #5 (realized-vs-lifetime)**
*Grounding: Media p.20 subscriber monetization (direct fit).*
cases.prompt_md: Vireno Media, a streaming service, is deciding whether to greenlight an expensive original series costing **$220M**. It is projected to attract **800,000 new subscribers** at **$15/month**. On first-year revenue the show looks like a money-loser. Greenlight or pass?

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Retention.
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Retention.** Annual churn on series-acquired subscribers is **30%/yr** (average lifetime ≈ 3.3 years). Discount at WACC 10%.

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: How would you structure this greenlight decision? Take a minute.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
Candidate must separate **year-1 (realized) revenue** from **subscriber lifetime value**. Flag if candidate judges on year-1 alone.

**Expected structure.**

Candidate must separate **year-1 (realized) revenue** from **subscriber lifetime value**. Flag if candidate judges on year-1 alone.

steps.label: first-pass (realized, year 1).
steps.candidate_md: What does the show bring in against its cost in the first year? Greenlight or pass?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
WACC=D('0.10')
subs=D('800000'); annual_rev=D('15')*12   # 180/yr
cost=D('220')
y1=subs*annual_rev/D('1000000')            # 144
naive=y1-cost                              # -76
```
Naive: 800k × $180 = **$144M** year-1 revenue, minus $220M cost = **−$76M** → looks like a **PASS**.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Do subscribers acquired by a hit series stay only one year?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Strong hypothesis: multi-year retention. The realized-only view ignores lifetime.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) Names the flaw precisely: the year-1 view credits the **800,000** subscribers with 12 months only — 800,000 × **$15** × 12 = **$144M** against a **$220M** cost — while the subscribers a hit series brings in stay beyond year 1, so realized revenue ≠ the value of the cohort. (2) Restates the correct object of valuation: lifetime value of the acquired cohort, discounted at **10%** WACC, over the period they actually stay. (3) Asks for the retention/churn rate and the horizon as the missing inputs, and states the direction — with multi-year retention the cohort's discounted value exceeds $144M and can clear the $220M, so the pass decision is premature.

**Fail if:** the candidate passes on the show because year 1 falls short of **$220M**, or swings to "subscribers stay forever" with no churn assumption and no discounting — an undiscounted perpetuity is the mirror-image error of the one-year view.

steps.label: Correct (lifetime, full multi-year chain — [4]+[9b]).
steps.candidate_md: Value those 800,000 subscribers over the full period they stay with Vireno, discounted. Where does the show land against its $220M cost?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
churn=D('0.30')
def ltv_per_sub():
    tot=D('0'); retained=D('1')
    for t in range(0,10):                  # 10-yr horizon, discounted
        tot += annual_rev*retained/((1+WACC)**t)
        retained *= (1-churn)
    return tot
ltv=ltv_per_sub()                          # 489.61
lifetime=subs*ltv/D('1000000')             # 391.7
correct=lifetime-cost                      # 171.69
```
Correct: LTV per sub = **$489.61** (discounted over retention), lifetime value = **$391.69M**, minus $220M = **+$171.69M** → **GREENLIGHT**.

hints.L1: Does a subscriber won by a hit stay only one year?
hints.L2: Ask what the retention curve looks like, then value the subscriber over the life it implies.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Sanity-check the number in your head. Over how long does a subscriber actually pay us, and what does that make the cohort worth against the price of the show?
steps.interviewer_md: **Expected mental estimate.** Sub stays ~3.3 yrs at $180/yr ≈ $500 lifetime (undiscounted ~$600, discounted ~$490). 800k × ~$490 ≈ $392M >> $220M → positive. The year-1 view is the trap.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: Your call is hanging on one assumption more than any other. Name it — and tell me how far it would have to move before you'd flip the decision.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) names retention/churn as the single swing variable, because subscriber lifetime is what converts the cohort into lifetime value; (2) tests it with a number: at **50% churn** (2-yr life) lifetime ≈ **$270M**, which still clears the **$220M** cost of the show; (3) gives the break point — the greenlight only reverses if churn exceeds ~**60%/yr** — and concludes the decision is robust once lifetime rather than first-year revenue is used.

**Fail if:** nominates price or the 800,000 subscriber count as the swing assumption instead of churn; or says "it depends on churn" without testing a churn level and without stating the threshold at which the answer flips.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Say the committee goes ahead. Give me at least six moves Vireno can make around this series to make the economics work — and group them for me.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups**, and the list must include: (1) reduce churn with a content slate built around the hit (2) tier pricing to raise ARPU (3) use the series to cross-sell the ad-tier (4) window international releases to extend the acquisition tail (5) merchandise / IP extensions (6) measure *incremental* rather than gross subscribers, to avoid over-crediting the show

**Fail if:** every lever is a first-year revenue or cost tweak on the $220M, with nothing that extends or protects the subscriber tail — and no idea that questions how the 800,000 subscribers are attributed to the show.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: The greenlight committee is waiting: do we make the series or not? Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Подписчик от хита остаётся только один год?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal retention: 30%/yr churn, ~3.3yr life.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Retention:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "churn" · "retention" · "how long do subscribers stay" · "lifetime value" · "LTV".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Retention', 'triggers': ['churn', 'retention', 'how long do subscribers stay', 'lifetime value', 'LTV']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Vireno should GREENLIGHT the series — on a lifetime basis it creates ~$172M of value, even though year-1 revenue alone looks $76M short."* Facts: 800k subs at $490 LTV = $392M vs $220M cost; the decision survives churn up to ~60%. Risks: (internal) the 800k acquisition and 30% churn are estimates — a soft launch could miss; (external) a competitor's rival hit could raise churn. Next steps: greenlight with a churn-tracking gate at 6 months; pre-commit a follow-on slate to defend retention.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask about retention/churn, not judge on year-1 revenue.
