cases.header_md:
## Case 84 — What's in the Box? (Sortwell) · M&A · **Hard** · Trap-flip · hypothesis-update

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** M&A · **Индустрия:** Logistics  
> **Difficulty:** 🔴 Hard · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap stranded (peak-capacity) · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Exhibit — Seasonality.; bar — Exhibit 2 — Load profile by hub and season
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① average view ② hypothesis-update ③ **peak-capacity, полный пересчёт [4]** ④ FLAG-checks + F6

**M&A · Logistics · Hard · Trap · naive #14 stranded (peak-capacity) · gen C**
*Registry: What's in the Box?*

**M&A · Parcel/logistics · F6 · Ловушка #14 (stranded — peak-capacity)**
*Grounding: Industrials p.22 capacity utilization — [DEVIATION NAMED: parcel sort-hub capacity + Q4 peak surge замещает book-to-bill].*
cases.prompt_md: Sortwell, a parcel carrier, is acquiring a rival. The synergy thesis: the combined network has **5 sort hubs of 300k parcels/day each** (1,500k total), but average daily volume is only **1,100k** — so management plans to **close 1 "redundant" overlap hub** and save **$15M/yr**, valuing the synergy at **$150M**. Is that synergy real? (WACC 10%, perpetuity.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Seasonality.
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Seasonality.** Q4 **peak volume = 1.30× average = 1,430k/day**. Full network capacity is **1,500k**. Premium third-party surge capacity for any peak shortfall costs **$0.20M per k/day for the season**.

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2 — Load profile by hub and season
triggers: how is volume spread across the day
exhibits.body_md:
| Hub | Capacity, k/day | Avg daily volume | Q4 peak volume | Peak utilisation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hub A | 300 | 245 | 318 | 106% |
| Hub B | 300 | 228 | 296 | 99% |
| Hub C (overlap) | 300 | 186 | 242 | 81% |
| Hub D | 300 | 232 | 302 | 101% |
| Hub E | 300 | 209 | 272 | 91% |
| **Total** | **1,500** | **1,100** | **1,430** | **95%** |

*Volume cannot be freely reallocated between hubs: each serves a fixed catchment, and rerouting adds $0.31 per parcel in line-haul cost.*
*The "redundant" hub is the least utilised on average.*

render.title: Exhibit 2 — Load profile by hub and season
head: Hub
Capacity, k/day
Avg daily volume
Q4 peak volume
Peak utilisation

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and walk me through how you'd structure your approach to evaluating this synergy.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Expected structure.** Candidate must test whether the hub is truly redundant — i.e., check **peak** volume, not just average.
🚩 Flag if the candidate accepts the average-based closure.

steps.label: first-pass (average view).
steps.candidate_md: On the volume management is working from, how much does closing one hub save a year, and what is that synergy worth?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
WACC=D('0.10')
hubs=5; hub_cap=D('300'); total_cap=D('1500')   # k/day
avg=D('1100'); hub_fixed=D('15')
# avg fits in 4 hubs (1200k) -> close 1, save 15
naive_saving=hub_fixed                            # 15
naive_value=naive_saving/WACC                     # 150
```
Naive: average **1,100k** fits inside **4 hubs (1,200k)**, so close 1 hub, save **$15M/yr** → synergy value **$150M**. Thesis works.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Is parcel volume flat across the year?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
Strong hypothesis: Q4 peak (holiday). The average hides seasonality.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) abandons the average framing explicitly — **1,100k/day is an annual average**, while a sort network must be sized to its **peak**; states the seasonality hypothesis by name (Q4 / holiday peak); (2) converts the hypothesis into the right test: after closing one hub capacity is **1,500k − 300k = 1,200k/day**, so the question is whether **peak-day** volume exceeds **1,200k**, not whether it exceeds 1,100k — the "400k of spare capacity" is spare only on an average day; (3) names the data request and the consequence — daily/weekly volume profile by season (peak-to-average ratio) — and states that if peak breaches 1,200k the **$15M/yr** saving is not free: it converts into peak-season overflow cost, and the **$150M** perpetuity value falls or disappears.

**Fail if:** the candidate keeps the average view, treats the 400k gap as genuine idle capacity and confirms the synergy; or agrees that volume is seasonal but never restates the test against the **1,200k** post-closure capacity, leaving the $150M unchallenged.

steps.label: Correct — peak capacity, full recompute.
steps.candidate_md: Work through what the network has to handle at its busiest, and tell me what closing a hub is actually worth.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
peak=avg*D('1.30')                                # 1430
# full network handles its own peak (sanity): 1500 >= 1430  -> True
# any single closure drops capacity to 1200 -> peak shortfall:
cap_after_1_closure=total_cap-hub_cap             # 1200
shortfall=peak-cap_after_1_closure                # 230 k/day at peak
surge_cost=shortfall*D('0.20')                    # 46 /yr  >> 15 saved
# every closure option is NEGATIVE; best = keep all open -> synergy $0
correct_value=D('0')
```
Correct: Q4 peak **1,430k** exceeds post-closure capacity **1,200k** by **230k/day**. Renting surge for that shortfall costs **$46M/yr** (one peak season a year), dwarfing the **$15M** saved. **Every** closure option is value-negative, so the best action is **keep all hubs open → synergy = $0**. The "redundant" hub is **stranded by the peak**.

hints.L1: What does the network have left once one hub is gone?
hints.L2: Put post-closure capacity next to the busiest-day volume, not the average one.

steps.label: Pressure-test your own answer.
steps.candidate_md: Push on your own answer before we close this out. Is there any version of this closure that does create value — and separately, is the combined network as it stands actually adequate?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) shows there is no partial-close escape — closing any single hub leaves capacity 1,200k, below peak 1,430k, a shortfall of 230k, and the resulting $46M surge cost exceeds the $15M saving; (2) states explicitly that no positive-value closure exists at the 1.30× peak factor; (3) separates the aggregate check from the hub level: in aggregate the network at 1,500k covers its 1,430k peak, and ex2 also shows Hub A at 318k of 300k and Hub D at 302k of 300k — a 20k/day overflow at two nodes. That overflow is NOT the same problem as the closure: the other three hubs carry 90k/day of spare in peak (B 4k, C 58k, E 28k), so 20k can be rerouted inside the network at $0.31 a parcel. **After a closure it cannot: capacity falls to 1,200k against a 1,430k peak, leaving 12k/day of spare against the 242k the closed hub carried in peak, and the 230k has to be bought outside.** Credit the candidate who spots the hub-level overflow AND says why it does not change the closure answer.

**Fail if:** the candidate claims a smaller or partial closure rescues the synergy, or asserts the aggregate 1,500k is short against the 1,430k peak — in aggregate it is not. Do NOT fail the candidate for saying two hubs individually exceed capacity in peak: ex2 prints peak utilisation by hub, so both nodes are derivable.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: You have the number. Now check it a second way, in your head: come at it per hub rather than per parcel, and tell me whether the sign holds.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) re-derives the answer by a different route than step 4 — e.g. per hub: one hub is 300k of capacity, the peak needs 1,430k, five hubs give 1,500k, so the network runs at 95% of capacity in peak and there is no whole hub of slack anywhere in it; (2) states that the $15M saving buys back 300k of capacity while the peak needs 230k of it replaced at a premium, i.e. we would be selling capacity at $50k per k/day and rebuying it at $200k per k/day; (3) reaches the same sign as the model and says so explicitly — the check is worth nothing if the candidate does not compare the two routes.

**Fail if:** the candidate simply repeats the step-4 arithmetic with the same numbers in the same order, or produces a second route that disagrees with the model and does not notice.

*The point of this step is not the number — it is that a $150M synergy is worth checking twice, and that two routes to the same sign is what makes it safe to say out loud to a deal committee.*

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: At what peak multiplier does the hub-closure synergy still hold? Give me the breakeven and where the actual figure sits against it.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
surge_per_k=D('0.20')                              # $M per k/day for the season, ex1
def synergy_value(peak_mult):
    pk=avg*peak_mult
    shortfall=max(D('0'), pk-cap_after_1_closure)   # k/day the 4 hubs cannot take
    net=hub_fixed-surge_per_k*shortfall             # 15 saved, 0.20 per k/day paid
    return (net/WACC) if net>D('0') else D('0')
# closure pays while 15 - 0.20*(peak-1200) > 0  ->  peak <= 1275  ->  mult <= 1275/1100:
breakeven=q(D('1275')/D('1100'),4)                # 1.1591
```
Two thresholds, and both are printed with their condition: below **1.09×** the closure is free and the synergy is the full $150M; between 1.09× and 1.16× it is only *partly* eaten — at 1.10× the shortfall is 10k/day, surge costs $2M against $15M saved, and the synergy is still worth $130M. It goes to zero at 1.16×. At 1.20× the shortfall of 120k costs $24M against $15M saved — stranded. At the actual **1.30×** the shortfall is 230k and surge costs $46M against $15M — stranded with room to spare. The entire deal-synergy hinges on the peak multiplier.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Give me at least six ways to capture part of the synergy without closing a hub, in at least two groups — cost side and capacity side.
steps.interviewer_md:
Capture partial synergy safely: keep all hubs but consolidate back-office/management (non-capacity cost), lease peak capacity to third parties in the off-season, invest to raise per-hub throughput (then close later), shift volume smoothing (pricing to flatten peak), sell one hub's real estate and lease back only for Q4, renegotiate the deal price down to reflect $0 hub synergy.

**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups.** Groups the ideas must span (at least two of three): **(a) cost synergy that is not capacity-based** — consolidate back-office, management and overlapping corporate functions across the two networks, keeping all **5 hubs** standing; **(b) monetise or reshape the peak** — lease peak capacity to third parties in the off-season, sale-and-leaseback of one hub's real estate with a Q4-only lease back, price to flatten the peak and smooth volume toward the **1,100k** daily average, invest to raise per-hub throughput above **300k/day** and close a hub later once peak fits; **(c) deal terms** — renegotiate the purchase price down to reflect **$0** of hub-closure synergy.

**Fail if:** the candidate re-proposes closing the overlap hub for **$15M/yr** / **$150M** in some softened form (close it partially, close it in Q1–Q3), or produces fewer than 6 ideas, or all ideas sit inside a single group — a list of six variants of "cut fixed cost at the hubs" does not clear the bar.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: You're in front of Sortwell's deal committee. What's your recommendation?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Sortwell should NOT count the hub-closure synergy — it is worth $0, not $150M, because Q4 peak volume (1,430k) needs the full network and any closure strands capacity."* Facts: average 1,100k fits 4 hubs but peak 1,430k exceeds 4-hub capacity 1,200k; surge to cover the 230k shortfall costs $46M/yr vs $15M saved; synergy survives only below a 1.16× peak and is whole only below 1.09×, and actual is 1.30×. Risks: (internal) the deal model likely bakes in this phantom synergy — revalue before closing; (external/regulatory) the acquisition itself goes to review, and any remedy on service coverage fixes the network cost base for years, and the back-office synergies we are recommending instead are the first thing such a remedy constrains — the revised price has to hold with them at zero too. Next steps. Within 30 days — strip the hub synergy out of the valuation model and reopen price on the revised number. Within 60 days — verify the 1.30× peak factor against three years of daily volume, since the whole synergy question turns on it, and scope the back-office synergies that do not consume capacity.

cases.difficulty_test: сеть держит собственный пик 1,430 при мощности 1,500, но закрытие любого узла опускает её до 1,200 — ограничение проявляется только в пике, и в ровном объёме его не видно
cases.gap_line: наив сравнивает мощность после закрытия 1,200k со СРЕДНЕСУТОЧНЫМ объёмом 1,100k и видит запас 100k: синергия $15M в год = $150M капитализации · верно: связывает пик Q4 1,430k, дефицит 230k в сутки покупается у третьей стороны по $0.20M за k/сутки = $46M в год против $15M экономии, поэтому отрицательны ВСЕ варианты закрытия и синергия $0 · разрыв $150M · механизм: ограничение, которого в наивной рамке нет вовсе — в ней мощность 1,200k среднее 1,100k НЕ СВЯЗЫВАЕТ, а связывающая величина, пиковый объём, в наивном счёте отсутствует

> **Слои insight:** ① average → marginal cost

**Cost Reduction · Chemicals · Easy · Trap · naive #7 avg-vs-marginal · gen C**
*Registry: Breaking Bad Batch*

**Cost Reduction · Specialty chemicals · F5 · Ловушка #7 (avg-vs-marginal)**
*Grounding: Industrials p.22 capacity utilization — [DEVIATION NAMED: batch reactor with idle capacity замещает book-to-bill].*
cases.prompt_md: Breakwell Chemical runs a batch reactor at **100,000 tons/yr** with **$30M/yr fixed cost** and **$200/ton variable cost**. A customer offers to buy an extra **20,000 tons at $240/ton**. The plant has spare capacity. On the plant's average cost the order looks like a loss. Accept or reject?

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd approach this order decision.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
Candidate must recognize the fixed cost is already covered by base volume; the extra order should be judged on **marginal** (variable) cost, not average. Flag if candidate uses average cost.

**Expected structure.**

Candidate must recognize the fixed cost is already covered by base volume; the extra order should be judged on **marginal** (variable) cost, not average. Flag if candidate uses average cost.

steps.label: first-pass (average cost).
steps.candidate_md: Work out the plant's cost per ton at its current volume, and tell me what that says about the customer's offer.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
vol=D('100000'); fixed=D('30'); var=D('200')
total_cost=fixed*D('1000000')+var*vol             # 50,000,000
avg_cost=total_cost/vol                            # 500/ton
extra=D('20000'); price=D('240')
naive_margin=(price-avg_cost)*extra/D('1000000')   # -5.2
```
Naive: average cost = ($30M + 100k×$200) / 100k = **$500/ton**. Offer $240 < $500 → order looks like a **$5.2M loss** → reject.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Before we put anything on paper — in your head, does taking that customer's order leave Breakwell better or worse off? Talk me through the reasoning, not the arithmetic.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) sees that the fixed $30M ÷ 100k = $300/ton of overhead is already carried by the base volume, so the extra batch does not add it again (2) states the extra batch adds only the variable $200/ton (3) concludes $240 > $200 → each extra ton contributes, so accept

**Fail if:** rejects the order because $240 sits below the plant's average cost per ton — the naive average-vs-marginal reject that the sign-check flips.

steps.label: Correct (marginal cost).
steps.candidate_md: The plant has spare capacity. What does it actually cost Breakwell to make those extra tons, and what does the order contribute?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
marginal=var                                       # 200/ton (fixed already sunk, capacity exists)
contribution=(price-marginal)*extra/D('1000000')   # 0.8
```
Correct: marginal cost of the extra batch = **$200/ton** (fixed unchanged, spare capacity). Contribution = ($240 − $200) × 20,000 = **+$0.8M** → **ACCEPT**.

hints.L1: Какой реальный дополнительный расход даёт лишняя партия, если завод уже работает?
hints.L2: Спроси, какие статьи себестоимости меняются с объёмом, а какие понесены в любом случае.

hints_en.L1: What real additional cost does an extra batch bring if the plant is already running?
hints_en.L2: Ask which cost items change with volume and which are incurred whatever happens.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: At what offer price does this order stop being worth taking? Walk me through the logic.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def contribution_at(offer):
    return (offer-marginal)*extra/D('1000000')
# breakeven offer price = marginal cost:
breakeven=marginal                                 # 200/ton
```
Breakeven offer = **$200/ton** (marginal). Any price above it adds profit; the $240 offer clears it by $40/ton. The order is accretive as long as spare capacity exists and price > $200.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Чем оградить базовые объёмы от новой цены и как убедиться, что мощность действительно свободна? Не меньше шести идей минимум в двух группах.
steps.interviewer_md:
Guardrails before accepting: ensure no cannibalization of full-price customers, protect against the price becoming a reference for future negotiations, confirm capacity truly spare (no peak conflict), check incremental logistics/energy cost, consider a short contract term, price-discriminate by channel to avoid margin erosion.

**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — commercial/price protection and operational/cost verification. Commercial side must include at least two mechanisms that stop the $240/ton leaking into the base 100,000-ton book: contractual protection against cannibalizing full-price customers, an explicit guard against $240 becoming the reference price in future negotiations, a short or fixed contract term, price discrimination by channel or geography. Operational side must include at least one verification that the incremental economics hold: confirm capacity is genuinely spare with no peak conflict, and check incremental logistics/energy cost on top of the $200/ton variable.

**Fail if:** the ideas are restatements of the accept logic ($240 > $200/ton variable, so take it) with no guardrail attached, or the list contains no mechanism preventing the $240 price from resetting existing customers' expectations — the one risk that turns a profitable 20,000-ton order into a loss on the 100,000-ton base.
steps.candidate_md_en: What do you fence the base volumes off from the new price with, and how do you make sure the capacity really is free? At least six ideas in at least two groups.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Breakwell's commercial director needs an answer on the customer's offer today — accept or reject. Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Какой РЕАЛЬНЫЙ доп.расход на лишнюю партию, если завод уже работает?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): state marginal = variable $200/ton (fixed sunk).
> - **Нет exhibit'а** (инсайт концептуальный). Раскрытие через hint-уровни. Триггеры: "marginal cost" · "variable cost" · "is fixed cost already covered" · "incremental cost".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Breakwell should ACCEPT the order — it adds $0.8M of contribution, because the relevant cost is the $200/ton marginal cost, not the $500/ton average."* Facts: fixed $30M is already covered by base volume; extra batch costs only variable $200/ton; $240 clears the $200 breakeven. Risks: (internal) accepting a below-average price risks anchoring future deals — keep it contractually one-off; (external) if base demand rises the capacity may no longer be spare, changing the marginal calculus. Next steps: accept as a fixed-term incremental contract, ring-fenced from list pricing.

> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should recognize fixed cost is already covered; ask for marginal cost of the extr

cases.title: Apocalypse Chow (Phorage)
cases.header_md:
## Case 86 — Apocalypse Chow (Phorage) · Market Entry · **Medium** · Trap-flip · open-drive

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** QSR  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap capacity · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Exhibit — Kitchen throughput.  
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① demand view ② open-drive reveal ③ **capacity ceiling + сверка [1]**

**Market Entry · QSR · Medium · Trap · naive #6 capacity · gen C**
*Registry: Apocalypse Chow*

**Market Entry · Vietnamese fast-casual · F1 · Ловушка #6 (capacity)**
*Setting: Vietnamese fast-casual (title dictates — "Chow"/Saigon flavour). Grounding: Retail p.13 throughput — [DEVIATION NAMED: kitchen throughput ceiling замещает footfall conversion].*
cases.prompt_md: Phorage, a Vietnamese fast-casual chain, is entering a new city with **8 stores**. Projected demand is **1,200 meals/store/day** at a **$12** ticket. City entry cost is **$60M**; store opex is **$3.5M/yr each**. On demand, entry looks very profitable. Should Phorage enter? (WACC 10%, perpetuity; stores trade **360 days a year**.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Kitchen throughput.
triggers: can the kitchen make that many
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Kitchen throughput.** Each kitchen makes **90 meals/hour**. Demand splits **70% into a 6-hour peak** and **30% into a 4-hour off-peak**. Meals demanded above throughput in any window are lost.

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

steps.label: Framework + open-drive.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd approach this — what are the pieces you'd want to look at, and which one would you start with and why? You're driving, so tell me the order.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) At least 3 MECE buckets that cover demand-based revenue, entry + opex cost (**$60M** entry, **$3.5M/yr** per store across **8 stores**), and competitive response. (2) States a hypothesis up front and justifies the starting point rather than listing buckets flat. (3) Before trusting the demand-based revenue, proposes to test whether the projected **1,200 meals/store/day** can physically be produced — kitchen throughput capacity — and treats that as the gating check.

**Fail if:** Candidate takes projected demand at face value — multiplies demand × the **$12** ticket and stops — or sequences straight to competitive response without ever testing whether the volume is deliverable.

steps.label: first-pass (demand view).
steps.candidate_md: Run the entry economics on the projected demand: what's the annual profit across the eight stores, and what is entry worth?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
WACC=D('0.10')
stores=D('8'); demand=D('1200'); ticket=D('12'); days=D('360')
naive_rev=demand*ticket*days*stores/D('1000000')   # 41.472
entry=D('60'); opex=D('3.5')*stores                 # 28
naive_value=(naive_rev-opex)/WACC-entry             # 74.72
```
Naive: 1,200 × $12 × 360 = $5.18M/store → **$41.47M/yr** across 8 stores; minus $28M opex → profit $13.47M → value **$74.7M** → ENTER.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update / open-drive reveal.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Can each kitchen actually produce 1,200 meals a day?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Demand concentrates in peak hours; the kitchen has a throughput ceiling.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) updates the hypothesis from demand-led to capacity-led: **1,200** meals/store/day is projected *demand*, and meals actually served = min(demand, kitchen throughput), so the revenue line built on 8 × 1,200 × **$12** is an upper bound, not a forecast; (2) names the mechanism precisely — demand concentrates in peak hours while the kitchen has a fixed meals-per-hour ceiling, so peak demand above that ceiling is **lost**, not shifted into off-peak hours, and off-peak spare capacity does not rescue it; (3) asks for the data needed to re-run the case: kitchen throughput in meals per hour, and the split of the day into peak and off-peak hours with the share of demand in each — and states the direction: served volume and the entry value fall, while the **$60M** entry cost and **$3.5M/yr** per-store opex are unchanged, so the entry call is at risk.

**Fail if:** the candidate keeps 1,200 meals/store/day as output and merely haircuts demand by a judgement percentage, or answers "we can add kitchen capacity / extend hours" without asking for the throughput ceiling and the peak split.

steps.label: Correct (capacity ceiling, [1] reconciliation shown).
steps.candidate_md: Demand isn't spread evenly across the day. Work out how many meals a store actually serves, and what that does to the value of entry.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
mph=D('90'); peak_h=D('6'); off_h=D('4')
peak_cap=peak_h*mph                                 # 540 (capacity in peak window)
peak_dem=demand*D('0.70')                           # 840 wants to buy in peak
peak_served=min(peak_dem,peak_cap)                  # 540  (capacity-capped)
off_cap=off_h*mph                                   # 360
off_dem=demand*D('0.30')                            # 360
off_served=min(off_dem,off_cap)                     # 360  (demand-capped, just fits)
served=peak_served+off_served                       # 540 + 360 = 900   <-- reconciliation
correct_rev=served*ticket*days*stores/D('1000000')  # 31.104
correct_value=(correct_rev-opex)/WACC-entry         # -28.96
```
Correct: peak window caps at **540** served (of 840 demanded); off-peak serves **360**. Total **540 + 360 = 900 meals/store/day** (not 1,200). Revenue = **$31.1M/yr**; minus $28M opex → profit $3.10M → value **−$28.96M** → **DO NOT ENTER**.

hints.L1: Can the kitchen physically produce the daily volume the plan assumes?
hints.L2: Ask for the kitchen's hourly throughput and how much of the day the peak occupies.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Before you do the precise arithmetic, ballpark it out loud for me: how many meals does one store actually get through in a day, and what does that do to the revenue line versus the projection?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) Peak 6h × 90 = 540, off-peak fills 360 → ~900 meals served per store/day; (2) states served volume is 25% below the 1,200 demand, so revenue ~$31M vs the demand-based ~$41M; (3) after $28M opex the perpetuity barely covers, and the $60M entry cost sinks it — sign-check: the capacity gap kills the entry.

**Fail if:** candidate takes the 1,200 meals/store/day projection at face value, never caps throughput at what the store can physically serve, and concludes entry is very profitable.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: How much throughput per hour would Phorage need for this city to be value-positive? Give me the number and what it means operationally.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def value_at(mph_):
    pc=peak_h*mph_; ps=min(demand*D('0.70'),pc)
    oc=off_h*mph_;  os=min(demand*D('0.30'),oc)
    rev=(ps+os)*ticket*days*stores/D('1000000')
    return (rev-opex)/WACC-entry
```
Entry needs roughly **104 meals/hour** throughput (vs 90) to turn value-positive — i.e., a bigger kitchen or faster line. At the given 90/hr the city is a loss.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Let's open this up. Give me six ways Phorage could still make this city entry work — and group them for me, don't just list them out.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups.** Book-level ideas: add a second line / more stations; pre-batch prep to lift peak throughput; smooth demand with off-peak pricing; add delivery-only ghost capacity; stagger store openings to test throughput; enter with fewer stores; relocate to lower-rent sites to cut the opex hurdle. Groups must genuinely separate the levers — e.g. throughput-raising moves vs demand-shaping moves vs footprint / cost-structure moves.

**Fail if:** fewer than 6 ideas, or every idea lands in one group, or the list is generic demand-building (advertise, promote, loyalty app) that leaves the kitchen's ability to actually produce 1,200 meals/store/day untouched — the naive capacity read.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Phorage's CEO is about to sign off on the city launch and wants your view first. What do you recommend?
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Кухня физически осилит 1200 блюд в день?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal throughput: 90 meals/hr, 70% in 6h peak.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Kitchen throughput:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "kitchen capacity" · "throughput" · "can the kitchen make that many" · "peak hours" · "meals per hour".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Kitchen throughput', 'triggers': ['kitchen capacity', 'throughput', 'can the kitchen make that many', 'peak hours', 'meals per hour']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Phorage should NOT enter the city as planned — capacity-capped revenue ($31M, not $41M) makes the entry worth −$29M."* Facts: kitchens serve 900 meals/day, not the 1,200 demanded; peak 6h caps at 540; entry needs 104 meals/hr throughput to work. Risks: (internal) throughput could be raised with capex — re-model before abandoning; (external) a faster-format competitor could capture the unmet peak demand. Next steps: pilot a higher-throughput kitchen in 1–2 stores; re-decide on measured peak-hour capacity.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask whether each kitchen can physically produce 1,200 meals/day.

cases.single_carrier_reason: носитель один по замыслу: вся числовая часть кейса — один связный объект (memo / таблица / график), и разрезать его на два экзибита можно только выдумав данные, чего цех не делает
cases.difficulty_test: Спрос упирается в пропускную способность кухни в часы пик: связывает физика линии выдачи, а не рынок.

cases.title: Mad Margins: Fury Road (Camburn Auto)
cases.header_md:
## Case 87 — Mad Margins: Fury Road (Camburn Auto) · Profitability · **Easy** · Trap-flip

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Auto retail  
> **Difficulty:🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap blended-vs-segment · **Время:** —  
> **optimal_entry:** 2  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Экономика в табличной форме
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① blended lens ② segment-level, вывести каждый

**Profitability · Auto retail · Easy · Trap · naive #2 blended-vs-segment · gen C**
*Registry: Mad Margins: Fury Road*

**Profitability · Auto-parts aftermarket retail · F5 · Ловушка #2 (blended-vs-segment)**
*Grounding: Retail p.13 (direct fit).*
cases.prompt_md: Camburn Auto, an auto-parts retailer, reports a blended margin across the group and three segments — Retail in-store, Online DTC and Commercial B2B (revenue and margin by segment: ex1). The board, worried about the "unproven" online channel, has proposed **closing Online DTC**. Should Camburn close it?

exhibits.title: Выручка и маржа по каналам
exhibits.body_md:
| Канал | Выручка | Маржа % | **Валовая прибыль** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retail in-store | $600,000,000 | 35% | **$210,000,000** |
| Online DTC | $250,000,000 | 42% | **$105,000,000** |
| Commercial B2B | $400,000,000 | 12% | **$48,000,000** |
| **Итого** | **$1,250,000,000** | **29%** | **$363,000,000** |

*Смешанная маржа 29% — средневзвешенная по выручке, не среднее арифметическое.*
exhibits.body_md_en:
| Channel | Revenue | Margin % | **Gross profit** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retail in-store | $600,000,000 | 35% | **$210,000,000** |
| Online DTC | $250,000,000 | 42% | **$105,000,000** |
| Commercial B2B | $400,000,000 | 12% | **$48,000,000** |
| **Total** | **$1,250,000,000** | **29%** | **$363,000,000** |

*The blended margin of 29% is a revenue-weighted average, not an arithmetic one.*

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: The board wants to shut Online DTC and they're asking us to sign off. Take a couple of minutes and lay out how you'd structure that decision — what you'd need to establish, and in what order. Start me off with where you think this lands.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) rejects the blended **29%** as a basis for the decision and states that a close/keep call is made on the segment's own economics — Online DTC runs the **highest** margin of the three at **42%**, above Retail's 35% and far above B2B's 12%; (2) states the correct test with the mechanism: profit lost if Online is closed = its contribution (**$250M × 42% = $105M**) minus costs genuinely avoided, plus what happens to the demand — whether it migrates to the **$600M** in-store channel at 35% or is lost outright; (3) at least 3 MECE buckets that include segment-level economics, the closure's second-order effects (shared costs and overhead that do not disappear, channel spillover), and the alternative use of the same attention — **B2B at 12% on $400M** is the real margin drag; (4) opens with a hypothesis, not with buckets — e.g. "we expect closing Online destroys profit; the problem sits in B2B".

**Fail if:** the argument runs off the blended **29%** ("Online is close to average, so closing it barely moves the number"), or off Online being the smallest segment by revenue; or the board's framing is accepted and the structure becomes "how do we fix/turn around Online" without testing whether Online is the problem at all.

Binary ask: *close Online DTC — yes or no?* Candidate must go to **segment-level** margins rather than judging by the blended number or by revenue size. Flag if candidate reasons from the blended 29% or from Online being smallest.

steps.label: first-pass (blended lens).
steps.candidate_md: Start with the overall picture: what is Camburn's blended margin across the three segments, and what does that imply for the board's proposal?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
seg={'Retail':(D('600'),D('0.35')),'Online':(D('250'),D('0.42')),'B2B':(D('400'),D('0.12'))}
tot_rev=sum(r for r,m in seg.values())             # 1250
tot_profit=sum(r*m for r,m in seg.values())        # 363
blended=tot_profit/tot_rev                          # 0.2904
```
Naive: blended margin **29.0%**. Online is the smallest, "unproven" channel — the board assumes it drags the average and proposes **CLOSE Online**.

steps.label: Correct (segment-level, derive each).
steps.candidate_md: Work out profit and margin for each of the three segments. What does that say about the board's proposal?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
for k,(r,m) in seg.items():
    print(k, 'profit', q(r*m,1), 'margin', m)
# Retail 210.0 @35% | Online 105.0 @42% | B2B 48.0 @12%
online_profit=seg['Online'][0]*seg['Online'][1]     # 105.0
```
Correct: Online DTC is the **highest-margin** segment at **42%** (vs blended 29%) — it is *lifting* the average, not dragging it. The real drag is **Commercial B2B at 12%**. Closing Online would **destroy $105M of the chain's highest-margin profit** → **DO NOT CLOSE Online** (kill→keep).

hints.L1: Маржа одинакова по каналам, или среднее скрывает разброс?
hints.L2: Запроси маржу по каждому каналу отдельно и посмотри, какой из них тянет среднее.

hints_en.L1: Is the margin the same across channels, or does the average hide the spread?
hints_en.L2: Ask for the margin of each channel separately and see which of them is pulling the average.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Just in your head now — which of Camburn's three segments is actually holding overall profitability down, and is it the one the board has in its sights?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) places Online at 42% above the blended 29% and states a segment above the blend cannot be the drag (2) identifies B2B at 12%, below the blend, as the drag (3) concludes the board is targeting the wrong segment — closing Online would pull the blend down, not up

**Fail if:** endorses closing Online DTC, or ranks the segments by revenue size instead of testing each margin against the 29% blend.

steps.label: Sensitivity / stress.
steps.candidate_md: The board doesn't trust the numbers behind your answer. What assumption would have to break for your recommendation to reverse, and how far off would it have to be before that actually happens?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) Names the Online DTC margin as the assumption to stress — i.e. asks what if it is overstated. (2) Gives the numeric threshold: it would have to fall **below the 29% blend** to be dilutive, a **13**-point error. (3) Concludes the recommendation (keep Online) is robust, and names **B2B at 12%** as the unambiguous diluter.

**Fail if:** Candidate says the conclusion flips on a small change, gives a directional answer with no threshold, or accepts the board's premise that a segment above the blend can be the drag / that closing Online lifts the blended margin.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Что делать вместо закрытия онлайна? Не меньше шести идей минимум в двух группах — по B2B и по онлайну.
steps.interviewer_md:
What to do instead of closing Online: fix/renegotiate B2B (pricing, mix, or exit), grow Online (highest margin, scalable), shift marketing spend toward the 42% channel, bundle B2B with higher-margin SKUs, analyze B2B's low margin (volume discounts? bad contracts?), protect Online's unit economics as it scales.

**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups.** Group 1 — act on the **Commercial B2B $400M at 12% margin**: diagnose why the margin is 12% (volume discounts, legacy contract pricing, service-to-serve cost), renegotiate price or contract terms, re-mix B2B toward higher-margin SKUs / bundle them in, or exit the worst B2B accounts in the limit. Group 2 — act on **Online DTC $250M at 42% margin**: grow it as the highest-margin channel, shift marketing spend into it out of the lower-margin channels, protect its unit economics (fulfilment, returns, CAC) as volume scales. Each idea must be a stated action attached to a named segment, not a topic heading.

**Fail if:** Any idea is "close Online DTC" — closing the 42% channel is the naive answer the case is built to reject; or fewer than 6 ideas; or all ideas sit in one group (only generic cost cutting, or only "grow online") with nothing acting on the 12% B2B margin.
steps.candidate_md_en: What do you do instead of closing the online channel? At least six ideas in at least two groups — on B2B and on online.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Camburn's board is about to vote on closing the segment. What's your recommendation?
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Одинаковая ли маржа по сегментам, или это среднее скрывает разброс?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal segment margins: Online 42% / Retail 35% / B2B 12%.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Segment margins:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "segment margin" · "margin by channel" · "break down the blended margin" · "which segment is actually low margin".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Segment margins', 'triggers': ['segment margin', 'margin by channel', 'break down the blended margin', 'which segment is actually low margin']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Camburn should NOT close Online DTC — it is the highest-margin segment at 42% and closing it would destroy $105M of profit; the real drag is Commercial B2B at 12%."* Facts: segment margins are 42% Online / 35% Retail / 12% B2B against a 29% blend; the board's blended-lens reasoning inverts the truth. Risks: (internal) Online margins must hold as it scales — monitor unit economics; (external) B2B contracts may be strategically necessary despite low margin — assess before exiting. Next steps: keep and grow Online; run a margin-recovery review on B2B before any closure decision.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask for segment-level margins, not reason from the blended 29%.

cases.difficulty_test: Сводная маржа дилера скрывает противоположные знаки по сегментам; кандидат сам решает, на каком уровне считать.
cases.lang_note: тег приведён к факту: тело на русском; перевод — отдельная волна
cases.single_carrier_reason: носитель один по замыслу: вся числовая часть кейса — один связный объект (memo / таблица / график), и разрезать его на два экзибита можно только выдумав данные, чего цех не делает

cases.title: Catch Me If You Scan (Swypeco)
cases.header_md:
## Case 88 — Catch Me If You Scan (Swypeco) · Pricing · **Medium** · Trap-overstate · hypothesis-update

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Fintech  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap flat-vs-tiered · **Время:** —  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Exhibit — Tier structure.  
> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① flat naive ② hypothesis-update ③ tiered, вывести каждый tier ④ **direction check: почему это OVERSTATE, а не флип**

**Pricing · Fintech · Medium · Trap · naive #3 flat-vs-tiered · gen C**
*Registry: Catch Me If You Scan*

**Pricing · Payments/fintech · F2 · Ловушка #3 (flat-vs-tiered)**
*Grounding: Banking p.12 fee/interchange economics — [DEVIATION NAMED: payment-processor tiered interchange замещает NIM spread].*
cases.prompt_md: Swypeco, a payment processor, handles **$20,000M** in annual volume and is considering a **+15 bps** take-rate increase. Management projects the increase applied to all volume yields a big revenue gain. Is that projection right? (Note: interchange is tiered.)

exhibits.title: Exhibit — Tier structure.
triggers: do large merchants pay the same
exhibits.body_md: **Exhibit — Tier structure.** Volume splits: **Small merchants $4,000M** (increase applies), **Mid merchants $6,000M** (applies), **Large merchants $10,000M** (on negotiated caps — increase does **not** apply).

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute — how would you structure your approach to checking whether that projection is right?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Candidate:**
Candidate must ask **which volume the increase actually reaches** — small vs large merchants are on different tiers. Flag if candidate applies the rate flat to all $20,000M.

**Expected structure.**

Candidate must ask **which volume the increase actually reaches** — small vs large merchants are on different tiers. Flag if candidate applies the rate flat to all $20,000M.

steps.label: first-pass (flat).
steps.candidate_md: Management applied the take-rate increase across the book. On that basis, how much additional revenue does Swypeco pick up?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
vol=D('20000'); inc=D('0.0015')                    # +15 bps
naive_gain=vol*inc                                  # 30.0
```
Naive: $20,000M × 15 bps = **$30M** extra revenue → raise the rate.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer: *"Do large merchants pay the same rate as small ones?"*
steps.interviewer_md:
**ЧТО ДОЛЖЕН ВЫДАТЬ САМ КАНДИДАТ (перенесено из поля вопроса):**
Strong hypothesis: large merchants are on negotiated caps the increase can't touch. Tiered structure.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) Rejects the flat application: **+15 bps** × **$20,000M** = **$30M** assumes every merchant re-prices, and names the mechanism from the interviewer's cue — large merchants sit on negotiated capped rates the increase contractually cannot reach. (2) Revises the hypothesis to magnitude, not sign: the gain is positive but **below $30M**, because only the un-negotiated tiers are addressable. (3) Asks for the volume split across the tiers — specifically how much of the $20,000M sits with large merchants — as the input required before re-sizing.

**Fail if:** the candidate accepts **$30M** and moves to implementation, or concludes the increase earns nothing. Also fail if the tiering is acknowledged but assumed to be a small tail — the case turns on the capped tier being the largest volume block, so a candidate who guesses the split instead of asking for it has not updated.

steps.label: Correct (tiered, derive each tier).
steps.candidate_md: Interchange is tiered — walk through the tiers in the exhibit and tell me what the increase actually earns.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
tiers={'Small':(D('4000'),True),'Mid':(D('6000'),True),'Large':(D('10000'),False)}
addressable=sum(v for v,ap in tiers.values() if ap)   # 10000
correct_gain=addressable*inc                           # 15.0
```
Correct: only **$10,000M (small + mid)** is addressable; large merchants' caps block the increase. Real gain = $10,000M × 15 bps = **$15M** — **half** the projected $30M.

hints.L1: Do all merchants pay the same rate?
hints.L2: Ask which merchant tiers the cap actually touches before applying it to the whole volume.

steps.label: Direction check (why this is OVERSTATE, not flip).
steps.candidate_md: Is the error in the direction of the decision or in its magnitude? Quantify it.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
overstatement=(naive_gain-correct_gain)/correct_gain*100   # 100.0
```

Raising the rate still **increases revenue** ($15M > 0) — the decision direction (raise) is correct. The error is **magnitude**: $30M projected vs $15M real, a **100% overstatement**. Tag: **Trap-overstate**, not flip.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Quick check in your head before we move on: does the increase actually reach all of the volume? What does that do to the projection?
steps.interviewer_md: **Expected mental estimate.** Half the volume ($10,000M of $20,000M) is capped and immune. So the flat projection is ~2× too high: real ≈ $15M, not $30M. Sign stays positive; size halves.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: Suppose management pushes the increase harder than 15 bps — how does the revenue gain scale, and does it ever get to the figure in their projection?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def gain_at(bps):
    return sum(v for v,ap in tiers.values() if ap)*bps
# gain scales linearly with the addressable $10,000M only; large tier never contributes.
```
Even doubling the increase to 30 bps yields **$30M** (still only on addressable volume), never the naive figure on full volume. The cap on large merchants is the binding constraint.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Give me six ideas for how Swypeco could still capture more of the gain it is chasing here — and group them for me rather than listing them flat.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups.** Book-level ideas: renegotiate large-merchant caps at renewal; add value-added services large merchants will pay for; tier the increase by merchant size; introduce a floor fee unaffected by caps; expand small-merchant volume (fully addressable); monetize data/FX rather than raw take-rate.

**Fail if:** fewer than 6 ideas, or all ideas assume the +15 bps lands on the full $20,000M of volume — i.e. the candidate never acknowledges that tiered interchange caps what large merchants actually pay — or the ideas arrive as one undifferentiated list with no grouping.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Swypeco's board asks what they should do about the take-rate. Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «Все мерчанты платят одинаковую ставку?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal tiers: large $10B on caps (immune), small+mid $10B addressable.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Tier structure:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "tiered pricing" · "do large merchants pay the same" · "negotiated caps" · "which volume is addressable" · "merchant tiers".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Tier structure', 'triggers': ['tiered pricing', 'do large merchants pay the same', 'negotiated caps', 'which volume is addressable', 'merchant tiers']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Swypeco should raise the rate — but expect ~$15M, not $30M, because half the volume sits on capped large-merchant tiers the increase can't reach."* Facts: only $10,000M of $20,000M is addressable; the flat projection overstates by 100%; large merchants are immune. Risks: (internal) even the $15M assumes no small-merchant attrition from the higher rate — model churn; (external) large merchants may resist any future cap renegotiation. Next steps: implement the increase on addressable tiers; model small-merchant price elasticity before finalizing; open cap renegotiation at the next large-merchant renewal.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask whether all merchants pay the same rate

cases.difficulty_test: Ставку поднимают на весь оборот, а часть его сидит на индивидуальных условиях: адресуемую базу выделяет кандидат.

## Case 89 — Yield of Dreams (Croplin Seeds) · Cost Reduction · **Medium** · **Clean**

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Cost Reduction · **Индустрия:** Agriculture  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Clean (validate no reversal) · **Время:** —  
> **optimal_entry:** 2  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Экономика в табличной форме
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① base economics ② **CLEAN-навык: проверить каждого кандидата в развороты** + F7

**Cost Reduction · Agriculture · Medium · Clean · naive — (validate no reversal) · gen C**
*Registry: Yield of Dreams*

**Cost Reduction · Agriculture/seeds · F7 · Clean (validate no reversal)**
*Grounding: CPG p.14 unit economics — [DEVIATION NAMED: seed-treatment line automation замещает SKU contribution].*
cases.prompt_md: Croplin Seeds can invest **$12M** to automate a seed-treatment line. It would cut **$2.4M/yr of labor** and add **$0.3M/yr of new maintenance**. Should Croplin invest? (WACC 10%, perpetuity.) *Check carefully whether there's a hidden catch.*

exhibits.title: Экономика автоматизации линии
exhibits.body_md:
| Статья | Значение |
|---|---|
| Инвестиции | $12,000,000 |
| Экономия на труде | $2,400,000/год |
| Новое обслуживание | −$300,000/год |
| **Чистая годовая экономия** | **$2,100,000** |
| WACC | 10% |
| Горизонт | бессрочно |

*Иных изменений в операционных затратах не предполагается.*

render_en.title: The economics of automating the line
head: Item
Value

exhibits.title_en: The economics of automating the line
exhibits.body_md_en:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Investment | $12,000,000 |
| Saving on labour | $2,400,000/year |
| New maintenance | −$300,000/year |
| **Net annual saving** | **$2,100,000** |
| WACC | 10% |
| Horizon | indefinite |

*No other changes in operating costs are assumed.*

steps.label: Framework.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and lay out how you'd approach this one. Tell me where you'd start and why when you're ready.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) builds a spine that gets to the net annual saving from the $2.4M labor cut and the $0.3M of new maintenance, valued against the $12M at 10%, with payback as a cross-check; (2) explicitly carries a validation branch, naming the specific catches to rule out — stranded labor (is the headcount actually removable), a capacity conflict elsewhere in the line, and an average-vs-marginal distortion in the quoted labor cost; (3) commits up front that if those checks come back clean, the arithmetic verdict stands — and closes by checking the structure works for the interviewer.

**Fail if:** candidate skips the validation and treats this as pure payback arithmetic, or manufactures a reversal the case does not contain and argues against the investment on invented grounds.

steps.label: Base economics.
steps.candidate_md: Work out the annual net saving from the automation, what it's worth at the given discount rate, and the payback period.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
WACC=D('0.10')
invest=D('12'); labor_saved=D('2.4'); maint_added=D('0.3')
net_annual=labor_saved-maint_added                  # 2.1
value=net_annual/WACC-invest                          # 9.0
payback=invest/net_annual                             # 5.7 yrs
```
Net annual saving = $2.4M − $0.3M = **$2.1M/yr**. Value = $2.1M/0.10 − $12M = **+$9.0M**. Payback = **5.7 years**.

steps.label: Validation (the Clean skill — check each candidate trap).
steps.candidate_md: Before you accept that number — what could reverse it? Name the specific catches you would test on a line like this, and tell me how each one lands here.
steps.interviewer_md:
**EXPECTED ANSWER:**
- *Peak-capacity conflict?* **No** — automation doesn't change throughput, so no seasonal stranding (unlike #84).
- *Avg-vs-marginal distortion?* **No** — a single uniform line, one cost basis (unlike #85).
- *Cannibalization / overlap?* **No** — one standalone line.
→ **Naive and correct converge.** There is no hidden reversal; the investment simply pays.

---

**Pass if ALL:** (1) names at least three specific candidate reversals and tests each, instead of accepting the $2.4M / $0.3M inputs at face value — stranded labour (does the full $2.4M actually leave, or does a share stay behind?), a peak or seasonal capacity conflict, an average-vs-marginal cost distortion, and overlap/cannibalization with another line; (2) rules each out on the stated mechanism: the line runs lights-out after automation so all $2.4M is removable; automation does not change throughput, so nothing is stranded seasonally; a single uniform line means one cost basis, so no average-vs-marginal gap; the line is standalone, so no overlap; (3) concludes that naive and correct **converge** — no haircut to the $2.1M/yr net, and the $12M at a 10% WACC stands on the base economics.

**Fail if:** the candidate invents a catch the case does not support — assumes a share of the $2.4M labour remains, or a hidden throughput/seasonality constraint — and marks the investment down; equally a fail if the validation step is skipped and the payback is simply restated without naming which traps were checked and cleared.

hints.L1: Пройди по строкам этой экономии по одной — какую из них ты не готов принять на слово?
hints.L2: Назови сам развороты, которые проверяешь на такой линии, и закрой каждый счётом.

hints_en.L1: Go through the lines of this saving one by one — which of them are you not ready to take on trust?
hints_en.L2: Name the reversals you check on a line like this yourself, and close each one with a calculation.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Rough it out in your head before we get precise — what does this automation earn Croplin in a year, and how does that sit against what it costs to put in?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) nets the labour saving against the added maintenance to $2.1M/yr rather than using the gross saving (2) puts $2.1M/yr on $12M at ≈ 17.5% return, ~5.7-yr payback (3) states this is comfortably above a 10% hurdle and confirms the sign is clearly positive — no trick is needed here, so invest

**Fail if:** takes the $2.4M/yr labour saving without subtracting the $0.3M/yr maintenance, or manufactures a hidden catch and rejects an investment whose sign is unambiguously positive.

steps.label: Sensitivity (one function).
steps.candidate_md: The labour saving is an estimate. How far would it have to fall before this investment stops creating value? Give me the threshold and tell me how comfortable that makes you.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def value_at(saving):
    return (saving-maint_added)/WACC-invest
# labor saving would have to fall below ~$1.5M/yr (net $1.2M) for value to hit zero:
breakeven_labor = invest*WACC+maint_added            # 1.5
```
Labor saving would have to drop below **$1.5M/yr** (from $2.4M) for the investment to break even — a wide **37% margin of safety**. The conclusion is robust.

---

### 🔍 Гипотезы разворота (перечень обязателен для Clean)

**Гипотеза 1 — застрявший труд.** Предполагаем, что часть экономии на труде не уходит с линией, и ищем долю, при которой вывод меняется:
```
2.4 − 1.5 = 0.9
0.9 / 2.4 = 0.375
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: чтобы вывод перевернулся, на площадке должно остаться более 37.5% сокращаемого труда — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 2 — стоимость нового обслуживания занижена вендором.** Предполагаем, что она выше заявленной:
```
2.4 − 1.2 = 1.2
1.2 / 0.3 = 4.0
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: обслуживание должно вырасти вчетверо — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 3 — ставка дисконтирования.** Предполагаем стоимость капитала выше напечатанной:
```
2.1 / 12 = 0.175
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: запас по ставке 7.5 пункта, поднимать её надо в 1.75 раза — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза «все проверенные стрессы ОДНОВРЕМЕННО».** Труд застревает, обслуживание дорожает и ставка растёт — всё сразу. Все три входят в одно неравенство:
```
NPV ≥ 0  ⟺  2.4 × (1 − застрявшая доля) − 0.3 × множитель обслуживания ≥ 12 × ставка
сегодня: 2.1 ≥ 1.2 — запас 1.75×
обнуление при одновременном движении: t = 33.3%
на трети пути (застряло 12.5%, обслуживание вдвое, ставка 12.5%): NPV = $0.00M
```
Гипотеза **закрыта, и это самый тонкий из проверенных случаев**: базовый NPV $9.0M положителен, но поодиночке кейс печатал запасы «до 37.5% застревания», «вчетверо по обслуживанию», «до 17.5% ставки» — а вместе достаточно ТРЕТИ пути по каждому. Настоящий запас — 1.75× по левой части неравенства, а не четырёхкратный.

*Метод: вводим единую долю t — все рычаги одновременно проходят долю t пути от фактического значения до СВОЕГО порога. при t = 100% все рычаги стоят на своих порогах одновременно. Запас по одному рычагу — не запас.*

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Before Croplin commits to this, what would you want to check or put in place to firm up the case? Give me six, and group them for me.
steps.interviewer_md:

**Fail if:** Fewer than six ideas, or a single ungrouped list, or the candidate manufactures a reversal that isn't in the case — the base economics (**$2.4M/yr** labor saved less **$0.3M/yr** maintenance against **$12M** capex at WACC 10% perpetuity) stand, and the brainstorm is about de-risking, not about overturning them.

steps.candidate_md: Croplin's CEO wants a decision on the automation investment. Your recommendation.

---

cases.header_md:
## Case 90 — Stakes on a Plane (Tailwynn Air) · Market Entry · **Medium** · Trap-flip · open-drive

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** Airline  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap wrong-ranking · **Время:** —  
> **optimal_entry:** 2  
> **Экспонаты (1):** table — Экономика в табличной форме
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① ранжирование по выручке → по прибыли

**Market Entry · Airline · Medium · Trap · naive #8 wrong-ranking · gen C**
*Registry: Stakes on a Plane*

**Market Entry · Regional airline · F6 · Ловушка #8 (wrong-ranking-criterion)**
*Grounding: Airlines p.19 RASK/CASK, route economics (direct fit).*
cases.prompt_md: Tailwynn Air, a regional carrier, can launch **one** new route. Three candidates: Route A, Route B and Route C (revenue and cost of each: exA). Management wants to pick the highest-revenue route. Which route should Tailwynn launch?

exhibits.title: Экономика трёх маршрутов
exhibits.body_md:
| Маршрут | Выручка | Затраты | **Прибыль** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Route A | $48,000,000 | $44,000,000 | **$4,000,000** |
| Route B | $36,000,000 | $26,000,000 | **$10,000,000** |
| Route C | $30,000,000 | $27,000,000 | **$3,000,000** |

*Запустить можно только один маршрут — ограничение по бортам и слотам.*

steps.label: Framework + open-drive.
steps.candidate_md: Interviewer offers: (a) revenue by route, (b) cost by route, (c) profit by route, (d) strategic fit. Candidate picks order.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) states a hypothesis up front that the ranking criterion itself is wrong — management wants the highest-**revenue** route, but with only **one** launch slot the choice must be made on profit per route, since **$48M** of revenue against **$44M** of cost is not the same asset as **$36M** against **$26M**; (2) structure has at least three MECE buckets covering route economics (revenue and cost per route, so a cost side is present), feasibility and capacity (aircraft, slots, crew — the one-route constraint), and strategic/competitive fit, framed as a mutually exclusive choice among A, B and C rather than a generic market-entry tree; (3) drives the case: names **cost by route (b)** — or profit by route (c) — as the first thing to establish, explicitly **before** any ranking, and defers strategic fit (d) to a tie-break.

**Fail if:** the candidate ranks on revenue and picks Route A, or opens on strategic fit (d) / market attractiveness before the cost side, or presents a demand-only framework with no cost bucket and no stated ranking criterion.

**Open-drive, ответ для ведущего.** Optimal: get **cost (b)** before ranking — revenue alone is the wrong criterion. Red-flag: rank by revenue and stop.

steps.label: first-pass (rank by revenue).
steps.candidate_md: Management wants the highest-revenue route. On the numbers in front of you, which one is it?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
routes={'A':(D('48'),D('44')),'B':(D('36'),D('26')),'C':(D('30'),D('27'))}
naive_pick=max(routes,key=lambda k:routes[k][0])    # 'A' (highest revenue)
```
Naive: Route A has the highest revenue ($48M) → **launch Route A**.

steps.label: Correct (rank by profit, derive each).
steps.candidate_md: Rank the three routes the way you would actually rank them, and tell me which one Tailwynn should launch.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
for k,(r,c) in routes.items():
    print(k,'profit',q(r-c,1))
# A: 4.0 | B: 10.0 | C: 3.0
correct_pick=max(routes,key=lambda k:routes[k][0]-routes[k][1])   # 'B'
```
Correct: profit by route is **A $4M, B $10M, C $3M**. Route B earns **$10M** — the most profit — despite lower revenue. **Launch Route B**, not A. Wrong-ranking-criterion (revenue vs profit) reverses the choice.

hints.L1: По какому критерию сравнивать маршруты — по выручке или по прибыли?
hints.L2: Запроси структуру затрат по каждому маршруту и сравнивай то, что остаётся после них.

hints_en.L1: On what criterion should the routes be compared — on revenue or on profit?
hints_en.L2: Ask for the cost structure of each route and compare what is left after it.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Run the three routes past me quickly in your head — what does that arithmetic say about management's pick?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) Route A's cost ($44M) nearly eats its revenue ($48M) → a thin $4M; (2) Route B keeps $10M of $36M (and Route C only $3M of $30M); (3) states explicitly that high revenue ≠ high profit — the cost line flips the ranking, so Tailwynn launches B, not A.

**Fail if:** candidate ranks the routes by revenue and picks Route A because it is the biggest top line.

steps.label: Sensitivity / stress.
steps.candidate_md: Stress your own answer for me. What would have to be true for your pick to change — name the assumption and tell me how far it has to move.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) names Route A's cost line as the swing variable and produces the breakeven — A's cost would have to fall below **$38M** (from $44M) to beat B's $10M profit; (2) sizes that as a **14%** cost cut and treats it as implausible absent a named lever, so B dominates; (3) states the ranking is robust to small revenue moves because the profit gap is wide — A $4M vs B $10M.

**Fail if:** candidate stress-tests revenue rather than cost, or declares the answer "robust" with no breakeven number attached — or re-ranks on revenue size and lands back on Route A.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Step off the numbers for a moment. Give me six factors beyond what's on the page that could sharpen how Tailwynn ranks these three routes — and group them for me rather than reading a flat list.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — expected content: load-factor ramp (which route matures faster) · competitive density on each route · aircraft utilization fit · connecting-traffic feed to the network · seasonality · strategic-market optionality. Candidate must also state that these refine the profit ranking but none of them reverse B's lead here.

**Fail if:** fewer than six ideas, an ungrouped list, or the candidate lets these soft factors overturn B's profit lead without evidence — or is still ranking routes on revenue.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Tailwynn's leadership wants one answer: which route do we launch? Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** ничего. Движок молчит и ждёт, пока кандидат сам выйдет на вопрос.
> - **hint_L1** (если застрял, после явного «не знаю, что дальше»): «По какому критерию сравнивать маршруты — выручка или прибыль?»
> - **hint_L2** (крайний случай, если L1 не помог): reveal cost by route: A profit $4M vs B $10M.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Cost by route:** `reveal_on_request`. Не показывать автоматически — только когда кандидат сам запросит. Триггеры-запросы: "cost per route" · "profit not revenue" · "route economics" · "what's the cost of each route".
> *Инсайт = добываемый, не преподнесённый. В interviewee-led режиме движок держит это закрытым; в interviewer-led (McKinsey-style) может подать L1 проактивно.*

---

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Cost by route', 'triggers': ['cost per route', 'profit not revenue', 'route economics', "what's the cost of each route"]}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Tailwynn should launch Route B — it earns $10M of profit versus $4M for the highest-revenue Route A, because revenue is the wrong ranking criterion; profit is."* Facts: profits are A $4M / B $10M / C $3M; Route A's high revenue is consumed by $44M of cost; A would need a 14% cost cut to catch B. Risks: (internal) the cost estimates drive the ranking — validate stage-length and fuel assumptions; (external) a competitor could enter Route B, compressing its margin. Next steps: launch Route B; monitor competitive entry and cost assumptions; hold A/C as contingencies if B's economics shift.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> Ключевой инсайт кейса кандидат должен **добыть сам**, а не получить в подарок.
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0 — тишина по умолчанию):** candidate should ask for cost by route before ranking; not rank on revenue.

steps.label: Framework + open-drive.
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and structure how you'd approach this. Then tell me which piece you'd start with and why — you're leading here.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) At least 3 MECE buckets covering the anchor's forward economics (**$4M/yr** revenue against **$6M/yr** cost, −**$2M/yr**), replacement-tenant / alternative-use economics, and the mall-wide footfall effect. (2) Starts with forward economics plus the alternative use, with a stated hypothesis for that choice. (3) Explicitly sets the **$20M** renovation aside as sunk and irrelevant to the go-forward decision.

**Fail if:** Candidate anchors on the **$20M** — treats it as a reason to keep the anchor, tries to earn it back, or wants to amortize it into the decision before comparing forward cash flows.

steps.label: first-pass (sunk-cost trap).
steps.candidate_md: Management's position is that they can't close the anchor after what they spent on the renovation. If they keep it, what's the annual result for the REIT?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
def q(x,n=0): return D(str(x)).quantize(D('1.'+'0'*n) if n else D('1'),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
anchor_rev=D('4'); anchor_cost=D('6')
fwd=anchor_rev-anchor_cost      # -2/yr
sunk=D('20')
```
Naive: "we already spent $20M renovating — closing wastes it, so keep the anchor." Result: keep losing **−$2M/yr**.

steps.label: Correct (sunk cost is irrelevant).
steps.candidate_md: Management keeps pointing at the $20M renovation. Take me through the numbers that actually decide this — keep the anchor or re-tenant the space?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
replace_net=D('1.5')            # in-line specialty tenants net +1.5/yr in the space
swing=replace_net-fwd           # 3.5/yr
```
Correct: the $20M is **sunk** — it's spent regardless. The only question is forward cash flow: keep = −$2M/yr vs replace with in-line tenants = **+$1.5M/yr**. Closing improves annual cash by **$3.5M/yr**. **CLOSE and re-tenant.**

hints.L1: Уже потраченные деньги меняют то, что выгодно делать дальше?
hints.L2: Ремонт потрачен при любом решении — сравнивай только будущие потоки двух вариантов аренды.

hints_en.L1: Does money already spent change what it is worth doing next?
hints_en.L2: The refit is spent whatever is decided — compare only the future flows of the two letting options.

steps.label: Mental-math check.
steps.candidate_md: Before any careful working — walk me through the annual cash comparison the way you would do it in your head, and be explicit about which figures actually belong in it.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) the anchor bleeds $2M/yr on a forward basis ($4M/yr revenue against $6M/yr cost) and keeps bleeding it indefinitely; (2) the alternative use of the space earns $1.5M/yr; (3) the $20M renovation is history — explicitly excluded from the comparison — so $2M loss vs $1.5M gain = clearly switch.

**Fail if:** candidate carries the $20M renovation into the decision, or argues the REIT should keep the anchor because it has already spent $20M on it.

steps.label: Sensitivity.
steps.candidate_md: Push against yourself here. What would have to change for management to be right about keeping it — name the assumption and how hard it has to break.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) identifies forward anchor cash as the only variable that decides this — the call flips the moment it turns negative, and it already is, at −$2M/yr; (2) shows the conclusion survives the harshest alternative case: even if re-tenanting netted only break-even ($0), stopping a −$2M/yr bleed still beats keeping, so the $1.5M/yr alternative is not load-bearing; (3) states the $20M renovation is sunk and cannot enter the sensitivity at all.

**Fail if:** candidate makes the answer hinge on recovering or amortising the $20M, or argues for keeping the anchor because closing would "waste" the renovation.

steps.label: Brainstorm (≥6).
steps.candidate_md: Якорный арендатор освобождает площадь завтра. Дай шесть вещей, которые можно с ней сделать, сгруппированных, и скажи, что проверил бы до решения.
steps.interviewer_md:
Say that anchor box comes free tomorrow. Give me six things Deadmall could do with the space, grouped rather than listed — and tell me what you'd want to check before committing to any of them.

**Pass: ≥6 ideas across ≥2 groups** — expected content: subdivide into in-line units · convert to experiential (gym/entertainment) traffic driver · medical/office conversion · last-mile fulfillment hub · pop-up/short-lease flexibility · ground-lease to a grocer. Candidate must also raise the mall-wide footfall impact of losing an anchor before finalizing.

**Fail if:** fewer than six ideas, an ungrouped list, no footfall check — or the candidate keeps the anchor because of the $20M already spent on the renovation.
steps.candidate_md_en: The anchor tenant vacates the space tomorrow. Give six things that can be done with it, grouped, and say what you would check before deciding.

steps.label: Recommendation (Pyramid).
steps.candidate_md: Deadmall's investment committee wants your call on what to do with the anchor space. Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
> - **hint_L0:** тишина.
> - **hint_L1:** «Влияют ли уже потраченные $20M на будущий денежный поток?»
> - **hint_L2:** reveal: $20M sunk, forward −$2M/yr vs replace +$1.5M/yr.
> - **Conditional exhibit — Replacement economics:** `reveal_on_request`. Триггеры: "alternative use" · "replacement tenant" · "what else could the space earn" · "re-tenant".
> *Инсайт добываемый. interviewee-led: движок держит закрытым; interviewer-led: L1 проактивно.*

---

**Conditional exhibits:** {'title': 'Replacement economics', 'triggers': ['alternative use', 'replacement tenant', 'what else could the space earn', 're-tenant']}

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

*"Deadmall should close and re-tenant the anchor — it stops a $2M/yr loss and the space nets +$1.5M/yr in-line, a $3.5M/yr swing; the $20M renovation is sunk and irrelevant to the decision."* Facts: anchor −$2M/yr forward; replacement +$1.5M/yr; sunk $20M does not enter the calculus. Risks: (internal) losing an anchor may dent mall-wide footfall — model co-tenancy clauses; (external) re-tenanting timeline/vacancy risk in a soft retail market. Next steps: run the footfall/co-tenancy impact, line up replacement tenants before closing, ignore the sunk cost in the board deck.

> **🎬 Interviewer-only disclosure (для движка, не показывать кандидату).**
> - **Что кандидат должен спросить сам (L0):** усомниться в аргументе «мы потратили $20M» — распознать sunk-cost fallacy и спросить про forward-экономику и альтернативное использование.
