steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide which family to close, and whether to close one at all?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis stated first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) a distinction between margin on the ticket and margin on the unit bought; (4) a closing question back to the interviewer.

steps.label: first-pass screen (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: From Exhibit 1 — which family looks worst?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Denim, ticket GM 58.00%** — the lowest of the six. This is trap #11: comparing at the wrong level of the metric.

steps.label: Realized margin (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Recompute margin per unit bought, allowing for sell-through and markdown.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Revenue = units×ST×price + units×(1−ST)×price×(1−markdown)
Denim:     120,000×0.80×68 + 120,000×0.20×68×0.70 − 120,000×28.56 = $4,243,200
Outerwear:  45,000×0.40×142 + 45,000×0.60×142×0.45 − 45,000×54.66 = $1,821,600
```
**Answer: the ranking FLIPS.** Realized GM: Denim **55.32%**, Outerwear **42.55%**. Denim is not the worst — Outerwear is.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Should Outerwear be closed? Avoidable costs are in Exhibit 4, the attach effect in Exhibit 3.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
NAIVE:   OH 2,285,000 − GP 1,821,600                      = +$463,400.00  → CLOSE
CORRECT: OH 2,285,000 − GP 1,821,600 − spillover 594,340  = −$130,940.00  → KEEP
```
**Answer: closing LOSES $130,940.00 a year.** The sign reverses. The swing of $594,340.00 is exactly the attach effect.

hints.L1: Does closing the line remove only its own economics, or does something leave with it?
hints.L2: Add the attach effect on the categories that stay before you compare avoidable cost with lost gross profit.

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why did ticket GM give the wrong answer twice?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** ticket GM measures margin on a unit sold *at full price*, while cost is paid on the unit *bought*. Sell-through and depth of markdown are the difference. Second layer: a family is not an isolated P&L — Outerwear anchors a visit in which $594,340.00 of additional goods is bought.

steps.label: Sensitivity (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what share of the attach effect does the decision reverse?

steps.label: Brainstorm (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What could be done with Outerwear instead of closing it?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass at 6 or more ideas in 2 or more groups: (a) buying/assortment — cut buy depth rather than the family; shift the size curve; (b) price/promotion — mark down earlier, in smaller steps; (c) attach — strengthen the link to Knitwear/Denim.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation to the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion in the first sentence with an action verb ("keep Outerwear, cut buy depth"); (2) at least 2 figures from the case; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: accuracy of the sell-through forecast; external/regulatory: a mild winter / seasonal demand); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

**Answer: the ranking changes.** The longest bar is not the costliest stage.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before you look at Exhibit 3 — what do you expect to find, and why?
steps.interviewer_md: Strong hypothesis: "expensive is not necessarily addressable". Weak: "mainline costs the most, so that is where we invest". Exhibit 3 confirms the first and breaks the second.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the 3-year net for each programme.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Crew:     703,248 × 3 − 2,450,000 = −$340,256.00   ← the naive pick, NEGATIVE
Mainline: 422,730 × 3 − 1,180,000 =    +$88,190.00
IX:     1,646,400 × 3 − 1,620,000 = +$3,319,200.00 ← correct
```
**Answer: Interchange handoff, +$3,319,200.00.** The naive pick destroys **$3,659,456.00** and does not pay for itself.

hints.L1: Does the programme earn back what it costs over the period it runs?
hints.L2: Net each programme's annual gain against its own upfront cost over the full three years before ranking them.

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Three screens gave three different answers. Why?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** bar length measures time, not money. Money measures the cost of an hour, but does not ask whose hour it is. Cost × addressability is the only metric that answers the question "where does the capex go".

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what addressability does IX stop winning?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Threshold: (net_mainline + capex_IX)/(IX stage cost × 3) = 27.6674%
  where IX stage cost is the annual stage figure, before the addressability discount
@30% → IX +$232,200.00 → IX wins
@20.728% → IX −$340,253.28 (threshold shown truncated) → tie with net_crew
```
**Answer: 27.6674%.** Solved against the same 3-year net as the main decision.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first; (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: IT readiness for EDI; external: the interchange partner's agreement / regulated access to paths); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Программы сравнивают по валовому эффекту, а срабатывает он лишь на адресуемой части парка.

cases.title: A Few Good Menus
cases.header_md:
## Case 133 — A Few Good Menus

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Fast-casual QSR  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Время:** ~31 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Меню-микс и юнит-экономика; table — Эластичность по позициям  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Pricing · Fast-casual QSR · Medium · Trap · ~31 min · naive #9 · gen E**
*Registry: A Few Good Menus*

**Type · Fast-casual QSR · F5 · Ловушка #9 (extrapolating a rate past its constraint) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: Chipotle · IO: Restaurant (labor — крупнейший кост, сырьё ~1/3 продаж), Kellogg p.227 · Layers: brainstorm, mental-math
cases.prompt_md: **Brantwell Kitchens** runs 12 fast-casual sites serving 486,000 guests a year. Input inflation is eating margin. The CFO proposes raising every price by 6%. What would that bring in?

exhibits.title: Elasticity by item
exhibits.body_md:
| Item | Own-price elasticity |
|---|---|
| Signature bowls | 0.4 |
| Wraps | 0.9 |
| Salads | 0.8 |
| Sides | 1.6 |
| Drinks | 1.9 |

*Guests notice the price of attach items — sides and drinks — more than the price of the main dish.*

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the effect of a price increase?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) volume response mentioned explicitly, not price alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass calculation + mental math (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Estimate the effect of +6% at unchanged volume, in your head.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Average check ≈ 0.42×13.50 + 0.22×11.00 + 0.15×12.00 + 0.14×4.50 + 0.07×3.25 ≈ $10.75
+6% × $10.75 × 486,000 ≈ $313,000
Exact: $313,397.10
```
**Answer: $313,397.10 a year.** Trap #9: a rate extrapolated across the whole base without the constraint that binds it.

hints.L1: Does a rate applied to the average also apply to every item behind it?
hints.L2: Build the average check from the mix first, then apply the increase to that, not to a headline price.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Recompute with elasticity by item.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
volume_after = volume × (1 − elasticity × 0.06);  CM_after = price×1.06 − food cost
Signature bowls: 204,120 → 199,221, CM $9.99 → Δ +$116,397.39
Wraps:           106,920 → 101,146, CM $8.03 → Δ  +$24,204.55
Salads:           72,900 →  69,401, CM $8.52 → Δ  +$22,674.82
Sides:            68,040 →  61,508, CM $3.42 → Δ   −$3,968.09
Drinks:           34,020 →  30,142, CM $2.80 → Δ   −$4,205.89
```
**Answer: $155,102.77 a year.** The direction is right — raise price — but the figure is overstated **by 102.06%**, roughly double.

steps.label: Explain + insight (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the distribution of the effect tell you?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** the gain is not spread — it is **concentrated**. The mains are inelastic and carry the whole effect; sides and drinks **destroy** value at +6%. The question stops being "how much" and becomes "where".

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: The loss is concentrated in the attach items. What would you do with the menu now?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: at least 6 ideas, at least 2 groups, at least 1 on price and 1 on cost/menu. Examples: (a) **price** — differentiated increase holding attach; raise bowls only; introduce a combo price; (b) **menu/cost** — cut the side portion instead of the price; reformulate the drinks input; drop the slowest SKU; raise the delivery price instead of dine-in.

steps.label: Targeted scenario (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out +8% on mains with attach untouched.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Answer: $213,125.39 a year against $155,102.77 on a flat +6%.
Gain from targeting: +$58,022.62
```

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what elasticity would it be worth raising the price of the attach items?

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first; (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: accuracy of the elasticity estimate; external: competitor response / input inflation); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Повышение цены оценивают на среднем чеке, а отклик у позиций разный: считать надо по составу меню.

cases.prompt_md: **Marrowfield Grocers** is an online grocer. It has budget to acquire 12,000 new customers. Where should they go?

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide where the 12,000 customers go?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) both retention and unit economics present; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Open drive (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Available to you: the cohort curve, zone economics, the household pool. Where do you start?
steps.interviewer_md: Optimal: cohort → zones → pool. Acceptable: zones → cohort. Red flag: going straight to "fix churn" without checking whether there is any.

steps.label: False trail (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the cohort curve say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: retention is IMPROVING.** The fall from 4.9 to 2.7 within a cohort is normal maturation; the plateau of newer cohorts is HIGHER than the older ones (2.70 against 2.20). **Churn is not the problem.** A candidate who rushes to fix it loses the case.

steps.label: first-pass screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: From Exhibit 2 — where would you grow?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Z5 Rural fringe, basket $102.00** — the largest → "grow the outer zones". Trap #10.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (7 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the CM uplift by zone, allowing for densification.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
New customers RAISE density → cost per drop falls for the WHOLE zone.
Gain = (on the new customers) + (on existing customers, now cheaper to serve)

Z2: density 28 → 42, cost $14.00 → $7.00
    on new customers 11,050×30×$11.72 = $3,885,180.00
    on existing 22,100×30×($11.72−$4.72) = $4,641,000.00
    Δ = $8,526,180.00 → $771.60 per customer
Z5: density 4 → 6, cost $26.00 → $25.00 → Δ $221,760.00 → $105.60 per customer
```
```
NAIVE:   everything into Z5 → absorbs only 2,100 → $221,760.00/year
CORRECT: by Δ CM per customer, filling in order:
         Z2 Ring suburb  11,050 × $771.60 = $8,526,180.00
         Z3 Outer suburb    950 (доливка, плотность 20 → 21.30) =   $427,485.00
         TOTAL                              $8,953,665.00/year
```
**Answer: the naive plan captures 2.48% of the best one.** Trap-action: expanding is right, the **allocation** is wrong.

hints.L1: Is the new volume all from outside, or does it change the cost of serving what we already have?
hints.L2: New customers change the cost of serving the existing ones in the same zone — count both sides of the density effect.

steps.produces: the naive plan captures 2.44% of the best one

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why did the biggest basket lose?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** basket is revenue, and the decision turns on margin after delivery. In the outer zone delivery consumes almost the whole gross margin ($26.00 of $26.52). Second layer: the gain is not confined to new customers — densification makes delivery cheaper for the entire existing base, and that effect is largest where density is already high.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What would reverse the allocation?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Z5 basket needed to match Z2: $187.38 (today $102.00) = +83.71% — implausible.
But the binding constraint is not the basket, it is the POOL: Z5 holds 2,100 of the 12,000 needed.
Even at an infinite basket the other 9,900 go to the dense zones.
```
**Answer: the constraint is the pool, not the basket.**
steps.produces: the constraint is the pool, not the basket

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first; (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: slot capacity as density rises; external: a competitor in the dense zones / delivery regulation); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Новые клиенты уплотняют маршрут и удешевляют доставку уже существующим: прямой счёт по новым верен и отвечает не на тот вопрос.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you value Norbrisk?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) an explicit distinction between one-off and recurring streams; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass valuation (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the backlog give you taken at face value?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
$840,000,000 × 4.00% × 9 = $302,400,000.00
```
**Answer: $302,400,000.00.** Trap #12: a stock — the order book — valued as though it were a stream of recurring profit.

steps.label: Firmness of the backlog (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Discount it for firmness.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: $639,090,000.00** of the $840M headline. Book-to-bill falls from 1.12 to 0.74 — the older orders are falling away.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before opening the memo — what do you expect?
steps.interviewer_md: The candidate's hypothesis is usually "discount the backlog and apply a multiple". The memo **confirms** the firmness discount and **breaks** the rest: even firm backlog earns 4%, and the value sits in after-sales, which attaches to the installed base rather than to the orders.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (7 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Now value it properly.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
One-off EBIT on the backlog: 639,090,000 × 4.00%          = $25,563,600.00
After-sales revenue:         9,400 × 58.00% × $11,500     = $62,698,000.00
After-sales EBIT:            × 31.00%                     = $19,436,380.00  (recurring)

CORRECT: 25,563,600 + 19,436,380 × 9                      = $200,491,020.00
ASK (seller: recurring EBIT × comp average 12.0× + one-off backlog):
         19,436,380 × 12.0 + 25,563,600                   = $258,800,160.00
```
**Answer: NAIVE says BUY ($302.4M > ask), CORRECT says PASS ($200.5M < ask).** Overstatement **50.83%**.

hints.L1: Is the backlog a one-off, or does something recur behind it?
hints.L2: Separate the one-off margin on the order book from the recurring after-sales stream, and value each on its own basis.

steps.produces: NAIVE says BUY ($302.4M > ask), CORRECT says PASS ($200.5M < ask)

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why can the backlog not be capitalised?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** a backlog is a stock — it is worked off once and gone. Applying a multiple to its EBIT treats one-off profit as perpetual. The recurring stream here is service on a base of 9,400 units, and that outlives any single order.

steps.label: Sensitivity (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what attach rate does the deal pay?

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not buy at the current price" / "buy below $X"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: our ability to lift attach; external: competition from independent service providers / parts regulation); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

**Type · Textile manufacturing · F5 · Ловушка #7 (comparing unit costs across different products) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: поставщик Levi's · IO: Industrial Goods (сырьё + человеческий капитал), Kellogg p.222 — *отклонение: первосортный выход (yield) — качающаяся переменная вместо after-sales* · Layers: mental-math
cases.prompt_md: **Ravenlow Mills** is a textile plant with 4 lines. The operations director proposes shutting Line C: "the most expensive cloth per metre". Do you agree?

exhibits.title: Avoidability and the alternative
triggers: what do we do with the capacity
exhibits.body_md:
**65.00%** of Line C's conversion cost is line cost and is avoidable on shutdown; the remainder is allocated plant cost — roof, boiler house, effluent treatment — which stays.

Alternative: re-tool C for Line A's staple cloth. Capex $640,000.00.

render_omitted.note: меньше трёх чисел, рисовать нечего

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to shut Line C?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) a question about which costs are avoidable; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass screen + mental math (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: In your head — which line is the most expensive?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Line C — the most expensive on BOTH denominators**, $1.62 per metre in and $2.25 per metre out. The naive answer is not an arithmetic error — it compares the **cost of lines making different products**. Trap #7.
steps.produces: Line C — the most expensive on BOTH denominators

steps.label: Contribution (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Look at what each line sells.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Line C: 648,000 × $7.50 + 252,000 × $1.40 − $1,458,000 = $3,754,800
        over 900,000 metres = $4.17 per metre in
Line A: $6,292,800 over 2,400,000 metres  = $2.62 per metre in
```
**Answer: the most expensive line is the most profitable per metre.** The $7.50 premium against $4.20 more than covers losing 28.00% to seconds.
steps.produces: the most expensive line is the most profitable per metre

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the effect of shutting it.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
NAIVE:   "we save the whole conversion cost of C"       = $1,458,000.00  → SHUT
CORRECT: avoidable 1,458,000 × 65% = $947,700
         947,700 − revenue 5,212,800                     = −$4,265,100.00 → KEEP
```
**Answer: shutting loses $4,265,100.00 a year.** A swing of $5,723,100.00, and the sign reverses.

hints.L1: Does shutting the line remove all of its cost, or only part of it?
hints.L2: Split the line's conversion cost into avoidable and unavoidable before setting it against the revenue that leaves.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what avoidability would shutting pay?
steps.produces: >100% is unreachable — NO level of avoidability justifies shutting

steps.label: The alternative (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What if C were re-tooled for the staple cloth?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
846,000 × $4.20 + 54,000 × $1.40 − $1.41 × 900,000 = $2,359,800.00
against C as it stands                                $3,754,800.00
A loss of $1,395,000.00 a year on capex of $640,000.00
```
**Answer: re-tooling DESTROYS value.** "Close the expensive line" and "re-tool the expensive line" are wrong for the same reason: rank by cost is not contribution.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first; (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: holding the 72% yield as volume rises; external: demand for the premium count / import duties); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

| Aggregator | 30.00% | **18.7%** |

*Weighted = 10.34%, which ties to the book. Aggregator: APR 27.60%, acquisition saving 0.90 pp.*
triggers_en: where do the customers come from

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the proposal to cut APR?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the seasoning of the portfolio raised explicitly; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Open drive (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Available to you: the vintage curve, balances and structure, channels. In what order?
steps.interviewer_md: Optimal: vintages → balances → channels. Acceptable: balances → vintages. Red flag: going straight to a margin calculation on the reported 6.10%.

steps.label: Seasoning (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: The reported 6.10% — can you trust it?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Shape of loss emergence from the three seasoned vintages (share of M36):
M6 15.5% | M12 43.5% | M18 68.5% | M24 87.0% | M30 96.5% | M36 100%

Projecting the unseasoned:
2024 H2: 9.1% at M30 → 9.43%
2025 H1: 8.2% at M18 → 11.97%
2025 H2: 6.6% at M12 → 15.17%

Balance-weighted TRUE loss = 10.34%
```
**Answer: 10.34%, not 6.10%.** Trap #8: the reported rate blends seasoned vintages with young ones that have not yet taken their losses.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the risk-adjusted margin at a 300 bps cut.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Margin = portfolio × (APR − funding 5.20% − opex 3.10% − losses)

NAIVE   at APR 20.90% and losses 6.10%  = $54,600,000.00 → CUT
CORRECT at APR 20.90% and losses 10.34% = $18,984,000.00 → DO NOT CUT
Today   at APR 23.90% and 10.34%        = $44,184,000.00
```
**Answer: the cut destroys $25,200,000.00 — 57% of what the book earns today.**

hints.L1: Is the printed loss rate the one this book will actually deliver?
hints.L2: Take the loss rate the issued book already carries once its vintages season, not the 6.10% printed.

steps.produces: срез уничтожает $25,200,000.00 — 57% того, что книга зарабатывает сейч

steps.label: Concentration (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Is the whole book deteriorating?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Channel-weighted = 0.32×6.0 + 0.24×7.1 + 0.14×7.9 + 0.30×18.7 = 10.34% ✓
Without the aggregator the book runs at 6.76%.
```
**Answer: it is NOT the book that is deteriorating, it is one channel** — 18.7% on 30% of the book.
steps.produces: портится НЕ книга, а один канал

steps.label: Third layer (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: So should they exit the aggregator?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Aggregator: APR 27.60% + acquisition saving 0.90% − 5.20% − 3.10% − 18.70%
            = margin on $252,000,000 = +$3,780,000.00   POSITIVE
Rest of the book: $42,672,000.00 on $588,000,000
Channel breakeven: 27.60 + 0.90 − 5.20 − 3.10 = 20.20% (today 18.70%)
```
**Answer: the channel is NOT loss-making — but it carries 30% of the book for 8.1% of the margin, on 1.50 pp of headroom.** The answer is not "exit" but "stop feeding it". Cutting APR hits precisely the thinnest channel, which is the opposite of what is needed.
steps.produces: канал НЕ убыточен — но несёт 30% книги ради 6.78% маржи при запасе 1.5

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you de-risk the channel without losing the volume overnight?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: at least 6 ideas, at least 2 groups, at least 1 on risk/underwriting and 1 on commercial/structure. Examples: (a) **risk** — raise the score cut-off to the branch level; cap the amount for first-time borrowers; verify income; risk-based pricing within the channel; (b) **commercial** — pay the aggregator on a performing loan rather than a funded one; grow branch and partner to replace the volume; buy-back on defaults in the first 6 months; switch off the worst partners and keep the best.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How fragile is the channel?

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation to the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not cut APR; tighten the aggregator"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: how fast the score cut-off can be tightened; external/regulatory: supervision of lending practices, aggregator response); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Каналы сравнивают по APR, а решает маржа за вычетом потерь того канала, откуда пришёл клиент.

cases.title: Rear Window Seat
cases.header_md:
## Case 138 — Rear Window Seat

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** LCC airline  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Время:** ~29 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** bar — BAR — экономика действующих маршрутов, недел; table — CATCHMENT — откуда берётся спрос на TSR  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Market Entry · LCC airline · Medium · Trap · ~29 min · naive #15 · gen E**
*Registry: Rear Window Seat*

**Type · LCC airline · F5 · Ловушка #15 (crediting displaced revenue as new) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: Wizz Air · IO: Airlines (load factor), Stern p.19 · Layers: hypothesis-update · *soft-trap: overstate*
cases.prompt_md: **Palterra Air** is a low-cost carrier based at Bergamo. A fifth route is proposed: BGY–TSR (Timisoara), 8 frequencies a week. What would it bring in?

exhibits.title: BAR — economics of the existing routes, per week

render.title: BAR — economics of the existing routes, per week
head: Route
Freq/wk
Load factor
Pax/wk
Fare
Cost/pax
CM/wk

exhibits.title: CATCHMENT — where TSR demand comes from
triggers: where do the passengers come from
exhibits.body_md:
BGY–TSR forecast: 8 frequencies a week, LF **82.00%**, **1,220** pax/wk, fare $63.00, cost/pax $22.00.

Origin survey of passengers on the existing routes:
| Route | Share from the Timisoara catchment | Passengers |
|---|---|---|
| BGY–OTP | 14.00% | 280 |
| BGY–SOF | 9.00% | 90 |

*Those passengers reach the hub overland today. With a direct service they would switch — and the routes they leave would keep flying the same schedule.*

render_omitted.note: проза с данными без табличной разметки — кандидат на ручную переверстку

triggers_en: where do the passengers come from

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the new route?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the question of incrementality raised, not the gross route economics alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass calculation (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the route give you taken at face value?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
1,220 × ($63.00 − $22.00) = $50,020.00/wk = $2,601,040.00/year
```
**Answer: $2,601,040.00 a year.** Trap #15: every dollar of revenue counted as new.

hints.L1: Is every dollar on that route new to the network?
hints.L2: Ask how much of the route's traffic already flies with us on another routing before calling it incremental.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before opening Exhibit 2 — what do you expect?
steps.interviewer_md: Exhibit 2 **confirms** that an 82.00% load factor is plausible — the network runs 79–91% — and **breaks** the assumption of newness: the Romanian routes share a catchment.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the incremental effect.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Displaced: OTP 280 × ($61 − $21) = $11,200.00
           SOF  90 × ($66 − $23) =  $3,870.00
                          total  $15,070.00/wk

NAIVE:   $50,020.00/wk = $2,601,040.00/year
CORRECT: $34,950.00/wk = $1,817,400.00/year
```
**Answer: the direction holds — the route is profitable — but the figure is overstated by 43.12%.** The routes left behind fly the same schedule, so their costs do not fall and the contribution is lost outright.
steps.produces: направление то же (маршрут прибылен), величина завышена на 43.12%

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why could you not simply take the route economics?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** route economics answer the question "is this flight profitable", while the board is asking "how much does the airline gain". The difference is displacement. With the schedule on the abandoned routes unchanged, a displaced passenger takes his entire contribution with him.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what switching rate would the route stop paying?
steps.produces: >100% недостижимо — маршрут прибылен при ЛЮБОЙ доле пересадки

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("launch it, but on $1.82M rather than $2.60M"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: accuracy of the load factor forecast on a new route; external/regulatory: slots at TSR, a competitor on the direct leg); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Новый маршрут забирает часть пассажиров у собственных рейсов: валовая выручка и приростная — разные величины.

cases.title: Good Will Hauling
cases.header_md:
## Case 139 — Good Will Hauling

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Growth Strategy · **Индустрия:** Last-mile logistics  
> **Difficulty:🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Время:** ~23 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Экономика сегментов за день; bridge — Избегаемость  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 3  

**Growth Strategy · Last-mile logistics · Easy · Trap · ~23 min · naive #14 · gen E**
*Registry: Good Will Hauling*

**Type · Last-mile logistics · F5 · Ловушка #14 (allocated fixed cost treated as avoidable) · Depth: LIGHT**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: XPO · IO: нет прямого спреда для last-mile; ближайший — Industrials (capacity utilization), Stern p.22 — *отклонение названо: stop-cost / плотность доставок заменяет capacity utilization* · Layers: mental-math
cases.prompt_md: **Vandreth Logistics** serves four segments out of a single depot. Finance shows the Grocery boxes segment losing money. Should they drop it?

exhibits.title: Avoidability
triggers: ask what leaves with the segment
exhibits.body_md: Dropping stops releases **$0.35** of driver time per stop. The depot, sortation and management do not change.

render_omitted.note: меньше трёх чисел, рисовать нечего

triggers_en: ask what leaves with the segment

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to drop a segment?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the avoidability of overhead raised; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass screen + mental math (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: In your head — which is the worst?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Grocery boxes, −$832.00/day.** Trap #14: an allocated cost taken for an avoidable one.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out what dropping it actually delivers.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Effect = stops × avoidable $0.35 − segment CM
Retail:   420×0.35 − 1,344 = −$1,197.00 → keep
Pharmacy: 180×0.35 − 1,008 =   −$945.00 → keep
Grocery:  640×0.35 − 1,088 =   −$864.00 → keep
Returns:  260×0.35 −   286 =   −$195.00 → keep
```
**Answer: dropping Grocery boxes LOSES $864.00 a day.** The segment covers $1,088.00 of shared cost that is not going anywhere.

hints.L1: Which of these costs actually disappears with the segment, and which stays?
hints.L2: Compare the avoidable cost per stop with the contribution the segment brings, segment by segment.

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why did the allocation give the wrong answer?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** the $1,920.00 does not disappear on exit — the depot, sortation and managers remain, and the cost simply moves onto the other three segments, making them look "less profitable" on paper at identical cash. Only $224.00 of driver time actually leaves.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what avoidable cost per stop would dropping it be justified?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Threshold = CM/stop = $1.70 (today $0.35)
@$1.00 → −$448.00 → keep
@$1.70 →     $0.00 → tie
@$2.00 →  +$192.00 → dropping is justified
```
**Answer: $1.70/stop — identical to CM/stop by construction.** A segment is worth keeping as long as the cost released per stop is smaller than the margin earned on that stop.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("drop nothing; raise price where CM/stop is thinnest"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: how Grocery customers react to a price rise; external/regulatory: fuel, drivers' hours); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Сегменты судят по полной себестоимости с разнесёнными $1,920 накладных, а отказ от маршрута возвращает лишь $0.35 водительского времени со стопа: вклад $1,088 уходит, возвращается $224.

cases.title: You Can't Handle the Tooth
cases.header_md:
## Case 140 — You Can't Handle the Tooth

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** M&A · **Индустрия:** Dental DSO  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Clean · **Время:** ~31 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Клиники цели; memo — MEMO — заметки due diligence  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**M&A · Dental DSO · Medium · Clean · ~31 min · gen E**
*Registry: You Can't Handle the Tooth*

**Type · Dental DSO · F5 · Ловушка #140 (CLEAN — validate no reversal) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: Smile Direct / европейские DSO · IO: Healthcare Providers (chair/bed capacity utilization), Stern p.16 · Layers: brainstorm
cases.prompt_md: **Ordwyn Dental**, a dental services organisation, is considering the purchase of a four-practice group. The seller presents the economics as straightforward. Should they buy?

exhibits.title: MEMO — due diligence notes
exhibits.body_md:
> (1) Denholm chair utilisation is 61% against a group average of 79%. The seller attributes this to a 2024 relocation: the practice moved 400 m into a larger unit.
> (2) Two associate dentists at Calderwood are on 12-month notice.
> (3) The group bills **14%** of revenue to a single insurer; that contract renews in 18 months. The insurer has served notice of a **repricing**, not a withdrawal — it is not exiting the region.

render_omitted.note: записка или реплика, render не положен

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to buy?
steps.interviewer_md:
Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the entry multiple named explicitly against the funding limit; (4) a closing question.

**Для ведущего.** *(Clean case: naive and correct agree. The candidate's job is to name and CLOSE the hypotheses of a hidden reversal with a calculation, not to say "the numbers add up".)*

steps.label: Base valuation (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the price tell you?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: 5.0× against a 6.0× limit and a 6.5× platform.** Rating arbitrage: $1,767,100 × (6.5 − 5.0) = **$2,650,650.00**.

hints.L1: Is a below-average utilisation a discount, or exactly what is being bought?
hints.L2: Put the entry multiple against both the platform multiple and the leverage limit, and read the spread.

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 1 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Denholm runs at 61% utilisation — is it dragging the deal down?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Denholm EBITDA $161,200 at a 13% margin — POSITIVE.
Without it the group makes $1,605,900, and the same 5.0× ask is $8,029,500.
Buying Denholm costs $806,000 and returns $161,200/year → payback 5.00 years.
```
**Answer: it is not dragging it down.** The hypothesis is CLOSED by calculation.

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 2 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Suppose the departing associates take **12%** of the discretionary book with them. What if the associates leave?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
The DSO holds the patient list; only the discretionary book walks — 12% of Calderwood EBITDA = $86,940.
Group → $1,680,160, entry = 5.26×
```
**Answer: 5.26× — below the 6.0× limit.** Painful but not decisive. CLOSED.

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 3 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: And an insurer repricing that takes **8 percentage points** off margin — what does that do?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
14% of revenue = $1,286,600; an 8% margin cut = $102,928
Group → $1,664,172, entry = 5.31×
```
**Answer: 5.31× — below the limit.** CLOSED.

---

### 🔍 Гипотезы разворота (перечень обязателен для Clean)

**Гипотеза 1 — полная потеря контракта страховщика, а не переоценка.** Предполагаем, что при перезаключении контракт не продлевается вовсе:
```
0.14 × 1,767,100 = 247,394
1,767,100 − 247,394 = 1,519,706
8,835,500 / 1,519,706 = 5.81
```
Гипотеза **закрыта поодиночке**: даже полная потеря крупнейшего контракта оставляет вход 5.81 против лимита 6.0 — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 2 — общая ставка стресса на обе уязвимые базы.** Предполагаем, что обе режутся одной ставкой, и сравниваем фактическую с пороговой:
```
(86,940 + 102,928) / (724,500 + 1,286,600) = 0.09441
(1,767,100 − 1,472,583) / 2,011,100 = 0.146446
0.146446 / 0.09441 − 1 = 0.551
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: фактический стресс составляет две трети порогового, запас 55.1% — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 3 — контракт теряется ЦЕЛИКОМ, и одновременно уходят ассоциаты.** Предполагаем худшее сочетание, какое допускают данные:
```
0.14 × 1,767,100 = 247,394
8,835,500 / (1,767,100 − 247,394) = 5.81
0.12 × 724,500 = 86,940
8,835,500 / (1,767,100 − 247,394 − 86,940) = 6.17
```
Гипотеза **закрыта — но с оговоркой, которую надо произнести вслух**: полная потеря контракта поодиночке даёт 5.81 против лимита 6.0, а вместе с уходом ассоциатов 6.17, то есть лимит пробивается. Напечатанный сигнал страховщика — переоценка, а не уход, и на переоценке в 8 п.п. худшее сочетание даёт 5.60. Вывод **не переворачивается**, но порог назван: лимит фондирования пробивается при потере более 83.9% контракта одновременно с уходом ассоциатов, и это условие цены, а не аргумент против сделки.

*Правило, купленное этим кейсом: кейс, который стрессует рычаги по одному и объявляет запас, обязан посчитать и худшее СОЧЕТАНИЕ — иначе он обещает запас, которого нет.*

steps.label: Combination + Sensitivity (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What if both stresses land together?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Both together → EBITDA $1,577,232, entry = 5.60× → still below 6.0×

Threshold: a COMMON rate applied to both exposed bases, not a scaling of the cuts above.
  bases: Calderwood EBITDA $724,500 + insurer-billed revenue $1,286,600 = $2,011,100
  at 14.6446%: cut $294,516.67 → EBITDA $1,472,583.33 → entry 6.0×
  at the 14.64% shown: entry 5.999627× (threshold shown truncated)
```
**Answer: 5.60×.** No reversal in any of the three directions, nor in the combination of the stresses as the memo sizes them. A full loss of the insurer contract — which the memo explicitly rules out, it signals a repricing, not a withdrawal — would combine with the associate departures to 6.17× and breach the 6.0× limit; that is a pricing condition, not an argument against the deal.

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What else could reverse the deal that is not in the numbers?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: at least 6 ideas, at least 2 groups. Examples: (a) **operational** — chair capex, IT integration, deferred maintenance, regulatory requirements on equipment; (b) **commercial/legal** — dentists' non-compete clauses, the lease and its renewal, litigation tails, dependence on a single referring dentist.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) a GO conclusion in the first sentence; (2) **an explicit statement that the absence of a reversal was tested** — three hypotheses run and closed; (3) at least 2 figures (5.0× entry, 5.60× worst case); (4) at least 2 risks (internal: integration and dentist retention; external/regulatory: renewal of the insurer contract); (5) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.qa_checks_md: **ВОЗВРАЩЁН В ВЫДАЧУ 08.08.2026.** Кейс был недоопределён: печатный стресс по контракту — переоценка на 8 п.п., а сочетание полной потери с уходом ассоциатов (6.17× при лимите 6.0×) кандидат мог построить законно. Сигнал страховщика напечатан, оба числа внесены в ключ.
cases.difficulty_test: Разворота нет: сделка проходит и по мультиплу, и по ковенанту, и это надо показать счётом, а не принять на слово.

## Case 141 — Cold Comfort Pharm

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Cost Reduction · **Индустрия:** Фарма-логистика (cold-chain)  
> **Difficulty:** 🔴 Hard · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** OK

**Cost Reduction · Фарма-логистика (cold-chain) · Hard · Trap · ~38 min · naive #6 · gen F**
*Registry: Cold Comfort Pharm*

**Type · Фарма-логистика · F1 · Ловушка #6 (fixing the stage with the biggest visible loss) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: региональный cold-chain оператор · IO: Healthcare/Pharma logistics — цепь 2–8 °C · Layers: multi-insight ×2, open-drive
cases.prompt_md: **Brayton Cold Chain** moves pharmaceuticals at 2–8 °C across East Anglia: 48,000 pallets a year at $12,500 a pallet. The board has released one capex slot. Where should it go?

exhibits.title: WATERFALL — spoiled pallets by link in the chain

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Per 1,000 excursion-hours the hub is worst (1.8333). **A plausible cut that decides nothing** — the hub stays first on both measures. The candidate has to work through this dead end and ask further.

steps.label: Layer 2: the fixes are not independent (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Of the 132 pallets lost at the hub, **54** are lost to the refrigeration failure alone. What if they do both?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Of the hub's 132 addressable pallets, 54 spoil at the doors ONLY because
they arrive with no thermal reserve. The refrigeration unit is a separate failure from the line-haul schedule, so fixing line-haul does not recover these 54 — they need the hub fix.

Line-haul fix           : 276 pallets →  $7,250,000   (unchanged)
Hub fix on its own      : 132 pallets →    $750,000
Hub fix AFTER line-haul :  78 pallets → −$1,275,000
Both together           :               $5,975,000  ← LESS than line-haul alone
```
**Answer: the hub business case is CONDITIONAL — it exists only if nothing upstream is fixed.** Approving both projects on their standalone figures counts the same 54 pallets twice.


steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the proposal to shrink the batches?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the cause of the defects questioned, not the correlation alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the scatter say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: defects rise monotonically with batch size, 0.75% → 2.00%** → "shrink the batches". Trap #5: defects are **detected** by batch but **created** by passes.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before opening Exhibit 2 — what do you expect?
steps.interviewer_md: Strong hypothesis: "a large batch is a different product, not a different process". Weak: "in a large batch a defect has time to propagate".

steps.label: Layer 1: attribution (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Attribute the defects to layers.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: defects per 1,000 unit-layers are EXACTLY 2.50 across all six runs.** Premium optics are ordered in volume and also carry more layers: **batch size is a proxy, layers are the driver.** The process is in control.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the effect of halving the batch on the premium line.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Defects = units × layers × 0.0025 — independent of batch size:
          96,000 × 8 × 0.0025 = 1,920 units at any batch size
Only setup changes: 30 runs → 60, i.e. +30 × $96,000 = $2,880,000

Batch 3,200: profit $103,776,000
Batch 1,600: profit $100,896,000
```
**Answer: halving the batch DESTROYS $2,880,000 a year and saves not one blank.**

hints.L1: Does batch size change how many defects arise, or only how often you set up?
hints.L2: Write defects as a function of units and layers, then see which term the batch size actually touches.

steps.candidate_md: Suppose we shift **24,000 units** of volume from standard to premium. So is premium at 8 layers unprofitable?

```

Premium      96,000     8     2.00%  $103,776,000   $1,081.00
Standard    240,000     4     1.00%   $65,712,000     $273.80
```

The answer is neither "cut batches" nor "cut premium" but **shift the mix**: moving 24,000 units of capacity is worth **+$19,372,800/year** (full restatement of both lines: new volumes → new defects → new run count → new setup).

steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to exit a channel?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the channel's contribution questioned, not the return rate alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the chart say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Marketplace returns the most — 4,200 units at a 15.00% rate** → "exit". Trap #6.

steps.label: Layer 1: what a return costs (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the unit economics by channel.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Marketplace has the HIGHEST CM on a kept unit — $427** — because CAC is $215 below the own site. And a return there is the cheapest of any channel (−$485 against −$700 on the own site) for the same reason.
steps.produces: у Marketplace САМЫЙ ВЫСОКИЙ CM удержанного юнита — $427

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out channel contribution after returns.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Own site       38,640×$389   + 3,360×(−$700) = $12,678,960
Marketplace    23,800×$427   + 4,200×(−$485) =  $8,125,600
Retail partner 17,280×$305   +   720×(−$430) =  $4,960,800
Wholesale      11,880×$109   +   120×(−$390) =  $1,248,120
                                        TOTAL $27,013,480
```
**Answer: exiting Marketplace DESTROYS $8,125,600 of contribution** — more than Retail partner and Wholesale combined. The channel worth discussing is Wholesale ($1,248,120 on 12,000 units).

hints.L1: Does the same order contribute the same in every channel?
hints.L2: Net returns off inside each channel at that channel's own return rate before comparing them.

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: A return costs $485 a unit and the channel still delivers $8.1M. What would you do about the returns?
steps.interviewer_md:
Pass requires ALL of: at least 6 ideas, at least 2 groups, both working on the $485/unit loss, none of them cutting the channel.
**Model set (8 ideas, 2 groups):**
> **A. Prevent the return (matching before purchase):** (1) a firmness test gated at checkout — ship the matched model, not the chosen one; (2) swap the comfort layer instead of returning the whole unit; (3) communicate the 30-day adjustment period before the trial clock starts.
> **B. Recover more value (after the return):** (4) a local open-box outlet above the current $236; (5) a hotel and charity channel for sanitised units; (6) break down to components — springs and foam back into production; (7) route the return to the nearest buyer rather than to the warehouse; (8) a restocking fee on marketplace orders placed outside the matching path.

steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("keep the channel, work on the returns"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: complexity of a matching gate at checkout; external/regulatory: marketplace return rules, the consumer's right to withdraw); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.prompt_md: **Meatharbor Foods** is considering the purchase of **Brawnley Processing**, which runs 420,000 head a year. Ask = 6.5× EBITDA. Meatharbor funds bolt-ons up to 7.0×. Should they buy?

|---|---|
| Head per year | 420,000 |
| Carcass weight | 340 kg per head |
| **Blended carcass price** | **$3.05/kg** ← the seller's metric |
| Revenue | $435,540,000 |
| Livestock + processing | $325,920,000 |
| Overhead | $18,900,000 |
| **EBITDA** | **$90,720,000** |

*Ask = 6.5 × EBITDA = **$589,680,000**.*

exhibits.title: How the carcass breaks down
triggers: ask how the carcass is sold
exhibits.body_md:
| Cut | kg/carcass | $/kg | $/carcass | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primal (loin/rib) | 56 | $7.50 | $420.00 | **annual contract** |
| Middle cuts | 94 | $3.50 | $329.00 | **annual contract** |
| Forequarter | 102 | $2.00 | $204.00 | spot |
| Trim & grinding | 68 | $1.00 | $68.00 | spot |
| Offal & rendering | 20 | $0.80 | $16.00 | spot |
| **Total** | **340** | | **$1,037.00** | |

*$1,037.00 / 340 kg = **$3.05/kg** — it ties to the headline. But **72.23% of the value** ($749.00) sits on annual contracts.*
triggers_en: ask how the carcass is sold

exhibits.title: MEMO — contract calendar
exhibits.body_md:
> (1) Both annual contracts are with two retail groups and **renew in 11 months**. They were signed in a drought year, when cattle were scarce and processors held pricing power.
> (2) The current market for equivalent primal supply is **$7.10/kg**. Middle cuts are $3.50/kg, unchanged. Cattle have got cheaper, three competitors have added kill capacity, and the premium is gone.
> (3) The livestock cost in the P&L is **already** at the current market. So are the spot cuts.

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the deal?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the durability of the EBITDA questioned, not the multiple alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the price tell you?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: 6.5× against a 7.0× limit** → "buy, it is inside the range". Trap #5: valuing on the metric the seller reports.

steps.label: Layer 1: what the blend is made of (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Break down the $3.05/kg.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: it ties exactly ($1,037.00/340), but 72.23% of the value sits on annual contracts** that renew in 11 months. Spot is already at market; the contracts are not.
steps.produces: сходится точно ($1,037.00/340), но 72.23% стоимости — на годовых контрактах

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out EBITDA after renewal.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Primal $7.50 → $7.10 (market), everything else unchanged
Carcass value $1,037.00 → $1,014.60 (−$22.40)
EBITDA $90,720,000 → $81,312,000 (−$9,408,000)

NAIVE  : 7.0 × today's EBITDA = $635,040,000; the ask of $589,680,000 is BELOW → BUY
CORRECT: 7.0 × post-renewal EBITDA = $569,184,000; the ask of $589,680,000 is ABOVE → PASS
```
**Answer: the ask exceeds the limit by $20,496,000**, and the contracts renew **inside the holding period**.

hints.L1: Is today's EBITDA the one the contract will deliver next year?
hints.L2: Reprice the primal at the market level first, then apply the multiple to the EBITDA that results.

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why was the blended price misleading?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** it averages cuts that are priced on fundamentally different terms. Spot already reflects the fall in the market; the contracts do not yet. The single figure hides that almost three quarters of the value is locked on terms that are expiring.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what primal price does the deal work?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
p* where 7.0×EBITDA(p) = ask → $7.2245/kg
@$7.50 (contract) → headroom +$45,360,000 → BUY
@$7.2245          → $0.00 → tie
@$7.10 (market)   → −$20,496,000 → PASS
```
**Answer: $7.2245/kg.** The market would have to recover $0.1245 of the $0.40 it lost.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not buy at $589.7M; bid no more than $569.2M"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: integration of kill capacity; external/regulatory: cattle prices, veterinary requirements, retail bargaining power); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Контракт на первичную разделку пересматривается по рынку: сегодняшняя EBITDA не та, что будет после продления.

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you check the market estimate?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the question of who the buyer is, not only how many there are; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass calculation (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Where does the $804M come from?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
24,000 farms / 8 years = 3,000 combines a year × $268,000 = $804,000,000
```
**Answer: $804,000,000.** Trap #4: market size taken from a population without the constraint that governs its use.

hints.L1: Does every unit in that population actually buy the machine?
hints.L2: State the constraint that governs replacement before turning the population into an annual market.

steps.label: Layer 1: who owns one (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Are all 24,000 farms buyers?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: only 3,624.** A combine is justified from 220 ha, and the average holding in the target regions runs 96–186 ha. The other 20,376 hire a contractor; there are 640 contractors running a fleet of 1,920 machines.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Rebuild the demand.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Replacement runs on ENGINE HOURS, not on the calendar:
  farmer     125 h/yr → 4,000/125 = 32 years → 3,624/32 = 113.25 units/yr
  contractor 500 h/yr → 4,000/500 =  8 years → 1,920/8  = 240.00 units/yr
                                                TOTAL     353.25 units/yr

NAIVE  : 3,000 units/yr = $804,000,000
CORRECT:   353.25 units/yr = $94,671,000
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME (the market is real), the overstatement is 749.26%.**

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why is the first-pass figure so far out?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** both errors push the same way. It counts all 24,000 farms as buyers when 3,624 own a machine. And it applies an 8-year cycle to farmers who, at 125 hours a year, replace once every **32** years. The contractors are the exception: their 1,920 machines generate 240 units a year, twice what 3,624 farmer-owners generate. **This is a contractor market, and the naive frame measures farmers.**

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What contractor utilisation would justify $804M?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
h* = 6,014.06 h/yr — 12.03 times the actual
and 1.50 times the machine's entire life (4,000 h). UNREACHABLE.
@400 h → $81,807,000   @500 (today) → $94,671,000
@800 h → $133,263,000  @1,000 h → $158,991,000
```
**Answer: the naive figure is unreachable at any plausible utilisation. The DECISION (enter) is robust; the SIZE has to be rebuilt from scratch.**
steps.produces: наивная цифра недостижима ни при какой правдоподобной загрузке. Решение (входить) роб

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("enter, but on $94.7M rather than $804M, and with a contractor-facing product"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: a dealer and service network built for high utilisation; external/regulatory: subsidies, grain prices, competitors with established contractor relationships); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Замена техники происходит по моточасам, а не по календарю: срок службы задан режимом эксплуатации.

```
Required inventory = $209,000,000 / 2.75 = $76,000,000
Release = $83,600,000 − $76,000,000 = $7,600,000
Holding saved = × 22.00% = $1,672,000/year
```
**Answer: $1,672,000 a year.** Trap #2: a saving computed off the average, with no regard for the distribution.

hints.L1: Is a one-off release of cash the same thing as an annual saving?
hints.L2: Work out the inventory released first, then apply only the holding rate to it.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Check how much of that is actually reducible.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
A: $14,400,000 × 0%  = $0          (cannot be cut — out-of-stock)
B: $21,000,000 × 5%  = $1,050,000
C: $19,200,000 × 10% = $1,920,000
D: $29,000,000 × 8%  = $2,320,000
                TOTAL  $5,290,000  reducible

Saving = $5,290,000 × 22.00% = $1,163,800/year
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME (the money is real), the annual saving is overstated by 43.67%.**
steps.produces: направление ТО ЖЕ (деньги реальны), завышение годовой экономии 43.67%

steps.label: Second pass: the one-off cash (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: And how much cash does it bring in immediately?

steps.label: Explain (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why was the average turn misleading?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** 2.50 is a single figure laid over bands that differ by a factor of 20 (8.00 against 0.40). The fast bands are already optimal and cannot be cut; the dead bands can be cut but do not convert to cash at book value. The average hides both.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What if the dead stock could be cleared at a better price?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
The $1,163,800 annual saving does not depend on recovery — the stock leaves the warehouse either way.
Recovery only affects the one-off cash:
@20% → $3,434,000   @35% → $3,782,000   @60% → $4,362,000   @100% → $5,290,000
```
**Answer: even at 100% of book, the one-off cash is $5,290,000 against the naive $7,600,000. No threshold is printed: the constraint is on volume, not on price** — only $5,290,000 is reducible.
steps.produces: даже при 100% книги разовый кэш $5,290,000 против наивных $7,600,000. Порог не печата

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("a programme worth $1.16M a year and $3.78M once, and the 2.75 target is not reachable by trimming"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: out-of-stock risk from trimming B, the P&L hit from writing down D; external: demand for obsolete stock, supplier terms); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Разовое высвобождение денег из запаса и годовая экономия на хранении — разные величины: какую из них обещали комитету, решает кандидат.

cases.title: The Vend of the Affair
cases.header_md:
## Case 150 — The Vend of the Affair

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Growth Strategy · **Индустрия:** Вендинг  
> **Difficulty:🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Clean · **Время:** ~26 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Предлагаемое размещение; memo — MEMO — существующий парк  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Growth Strategy · Вендинг · Easy · Clean · ~26 min · gen F**
*Registry: The Vend of the Affair*

**Type · Вендинг · F5 · Ловушка #150 (CLEAN — validate no reversal) · Depth: LIGHT**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: оператор unattended retail · IO: Retail — выручка на автомат-день · Layers: mental-math
cases.prompt_md: **Vantrode Machines** proposes placing 240 new machines across four site types. The economics are presented as straightforward. Should they launch?

exhibits.title: Proposed placement
triggers: what does each site type earn
exhibits.body_md:
| Site type | Machines | Revenue/machine-day | Gross margin | Annual revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transport hubs | 60 | $42.00 | 58.00% | $919,800 |
| Office lobbies | 90 | $26.00 | 62.00% | $854,100 |
| Hospitals | 50 | $34.00 | 60.00% | $620,500 |
| Campuses | 40 | $30.00 | 61.00% | $438,000 |
| **Total** | **240** | | | **$2,832,400** |

*Machine $7,400 installed · servicing $2,600 per machine per year (restocking, cash collection, repair).*
triggers_en: what does each site type earn

exhibits.title: MEMO — the existing estate
triggers: ask about the machines we already have
exhibits.body_md:
> The existing estate is **310** machines at **$28.00** per machine-day and a gross margin of **60.00%**.
> Commercial's estimate: the new sites will take **4.00%** of the existing estate's revenue.

render_omitted.note: записка или реплика, render не положен

triggers_en: ask about the machines we already have

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to launch?
steps.interviewer_md:
Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) **the hypotheses of a possible reversal named explicitly**; (4) a closing question.

**Для ведущего.** *(Clean case: naive and correct agree — GO. The candidate's job is to NAME the hypotheses of a hidden reversal and CLOSE each one with a calculation, not to say "the numbers add up".)*

steps.label: Base case (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the base case.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Revenue $2,832,400 · gross profit $1,702,506
Servicing 240 × $2,600 = $624,000
Annual profit $1,078,506
Capex 240 × $7,400 = $1,776,000 → payback ~1.65 years
```
**Answer: all four site types are profitable. Naive and correct AGREE: GO.**
steps.produces: все четыре типа точек прибыльны. Наив и correct СОВПАДАЮТ: GO

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 1 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Is the weakest site type dragging the case down?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Campuses: $163,180 on 40 machines — POSITIVE
Without them: profit $915,326, capex $1,480,000, payback ~1.62 against ~1.65
```
**Answer: it neither drags nor carries. CLOSED by calculation.**

hints.L1: Is the weakest site type dragging the case, or is its share negligible? Settle it by calculation.
hints.L2: Recompute the case with the weakest site type removed and see whether the verdict actually moves.

steps.produces: не тянет и не тащит. ЗАКРЫТА расчётом

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 2 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What about cannibalising the existing estate?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Existing estate: 310 × $28.00 × 365 = $3,168,200
Losing 4.00% of revenue × 60.00% margin = $76,036.80
Project profit: $1,078,506 → $1,002,469.20, payback ~1.77
```
**Answer: cannibalisation costs 7.05% of the uplift — not a reversal. CLOSED.**
steps.produces: каннибализация стоит 7.05% прироста — не разворот. ЗАКРЫТА

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 3 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Servicing goes from $2,600 to $3,400 per machine per year — new routes, vans, staff. Does that close the case or open it?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Stress $2,600 → $3,400 per machine per year (+30.77%):
  profit $1,078,506 → $886,506, payback ~2.00
  Transport hubs, offices, hospitals, campuses — ALL remain positive
```
**Answer: CLOSED.**

---

### 🔍 Гипотезы разворота (перечень обязателен для Clean)

**Гипотеза 1 — каннибализация занижена в разы.** Предполагаем, что новые точки съедают больше заявленного, и ищем порог:
```
3,168,200 × 0.01 × 0.60 = 19,009.20
1,078,506 / 19,009.20 = 56.74
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: чтобы убить проект, новые автоматы должны отобрать 56.74% выручки существующего парка против замеренных 4% — запас в 14 раз, вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 2 — площадки работают не круглый год.** Предполагаем, что офисы и кампусы простаивают, и считаем, сколько дней достаточно:
```
624,000 / 1,702,506 = 0.3665
0.3665 × 365 = 134
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: даже при работе 134 дня в году валовая прибыль покрывает обслуживание — вывод **не переворачивается**.

**Гипотеза 3 — оба стресса приходят вместе.** Предполагаем подорожание обслуживания и каннибализацию одновременно:
```
1,078,506 − 240 × 800 − 76,036.80 = 810,469.20
1,776,000 / 810,469.20 = 2.19
```
Гипотеза **закрыта**: совместный стресс удлиняет окупаемость с 1.65 до 2.19 года и оставляет $810,469 — вывод **не переворачивается**.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what annual servicing cost per machine does the profit go to zero, and how much headroom is that?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Breakeven servicing = $1,702,506 / 240 = $7,093.775 per machine per year
(this is NOT $7,093.78 — the value sits on a half-cent; the control points are computed from the exact figure)
@$2,600 → $1,078,506   @$3,400 → $886,506   @$7,093.775 → $0.00   @$9,000 → −$457,494
```
**Answer: 172.84% of headroom on servicing cost.**

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) a GO conclusion in the first sentence; (2) **an explicit statement that the absence of a reversal was tested** — three hypotheses run and closed; (3) at least 2 figures ($1,078,506/year, payback ~1.65, headroom 172.84%); (4) at least 2 risks (internal: restocking logistics as the estate grows; external/regulatory: site leases, regulation of vending in hospitals); (5) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Разворота в кейсе нет, и кандидат обязан это доказать: назвать каждую гипотезу разворота и закрыть её счётом.

steps.label: Framework (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to pay for Caldwyn?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the synergy tested for PHYSICAL feasibility rather than taken from the thesis; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass synergy (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the synergy on the deal thesis.
steps.produces: $20,700,000 — это наив #7. Он предполагает, что мощность есть

steps.label: CORE: what physically fits (7 min)
steps.candidate_md: Check whether that volume fits.

```
Molecular   needs 62,000 h, free  3,000 → takes   57,000 tests
Immunoassay needs 15,200 h, free 21,600 → takes  380,000
Chemistry   needs  6,050 h, free 25,200 → takes  242,000
                                    TOTAL   679,000 of 1,800,000

Real synergy = 679,000 × $11.50 = $7,808,500/year
Overstatement: 165.10%
```

steps.label: The decision at the funding limit (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: What can Perrivane pay?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
                        Sustainable EBITDA   Max price at 9.0×    vs ask $273,120,000
NAIVE                      $34,140,000        $307,260,000            BUY
What fits today            $21,248,500        $191,236,500       PASS (−$81,883,500)
```
**Answer: on what fits, the deal does not clear.**

steps.label: Layer 2: buy the capacity (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: And if they buy more molecular analysers?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Shortfall 59,000 hours → 10 analysers (60,000 h)
Full synergy $20,700,000 − opex 10 × $310,000 = $17,600,000/year
Max price = 9.0 × ($13,440,000 + $17,600,000) = $279,360,000
Headroom over the ask: +$6,240,000 — BUT capex 10 × $1,450,000 = $14,500,000
TRUE headroom: −$8,260,000
```
**Answer: PASS. The capacity is real but not free — capex the naive model never had.**

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what price does the deal work?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
ask $240,000,000 → headroom  $24,860,000 → BUY
ask $264,860,000 → headroom           $0 → tie
ask $273,120,000 → headroom  −$8,260,000 → PASS
```
**Answer: the breakeven ask is $264,860,000 — negotiate $8,260,000 off or walk. No threshold on UTILISATION is printed: once the analysers are bought, the synergy is capped by the outsourced volume and the function goes flat.**
steps.produces: безубыточный ask $264,860,000 — сторговать $8,260,000 либо уходить. Порог по ЗАГРУЗКЕ

steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the committee.

exhibits.body_md:

steps.label: first-pass choice (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does load factor say?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Lakes Run — 70.00% against Northline's 90.00%
Naive #11: cut Lakes Run, move the capacity to Northline
```
**Answer: this is the naive read. Load factor measures how full a train is, not what the fleet returns.**
steps.produces: это наив. Загрузка меряет заполнение поезда, а не отдачу флота

steps.label: CORE: contribution per carriage-day (7 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the return on the scarce asset.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Route        Revenue       Operating     Fleet        Contribution  $/carriage-day
Northline    $20,779,200   $10,920,000   $5,616,000   $4,243,200        $340
Coastway      $7,463,520    $5,256,000   $1,478,250     $729,270        $222
Highland     $13,378,560    $7,488,000   $5,616,000     $274,560         $22
Lakes Run     $6,988,800    $4,992,000   $1,404,000     $592,800        $190
TOTAL                                                 $5,839,830

Load factor:   Northline > Coastway = Highland > Lakes Run
Carriage-day:  Northline > Coastway > Lakes Run > Highland
```
**Answer: the two rankings DIVERGE. Lakes Run is second on return to the asset, not the worst. The route to examine is Highland: 80% load factor looks healthy, but $22 a carriage-day, because it holds 15 carriages for 4 days (60 carriage-days against Lakes Run's 10).**

hints.L1: Are you counting per route, or per unit of the scarce asset?
hints.L2: Divide each route's contribution by the fleet it ties up, not by the revenue it books.

steps.produces: два ранжирования РАСХОДЯТСЯ. Lakes Run — второй по отдаче на актив, а не худший. Пров

steps.label: What the first-pass plan actually does (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work the redeployment through.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Closing Lakes Run frees 3,120 carriage-days
Northline: 24 carriage-days per departure → 130 extra departures

But Northline leaves only 12,480 berth-nights unsold,
while 130 departures add 130 × 240 = 31,200 berth-nights — 2.50× the visible demand.
New berths fill at the MARGINAL load factor of 55%, not at 90%.

  17,160 berths × $185 = $3,174,600
  − operating $2,730,000 − fleet $1,404,000 = −$959,400

NET effect of the move: −$959,400 − $592,800 = −$1,552,200
```
**Answer: the naive plan destroys $1,552,200 a year.**

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what load factor would the redeployment pay?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
lf* = 81.8919% (repeating, shown to 4 decimals)
  55.00% → −$1,552,200 → destroys
  70.00% →   −$686,400 → destroys
  81.89% →           $0 → tie
  95.00% →   +$756,600 → pays
```
**Answer: 81.8919% is BELOW the route's overall 90% — which is exactly why the naive plan looks plausible. The question is whether 130 ADDITIONAL departures fill like established ones, when supply would exceed visible demand by 2.50×.**
steps.produces: 81.8919% НИЖЕ общих 90% маршрута — именно поэтому наивный план выглядит правдоподобно

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — keep Lakes Run, re-examine Highland; (2) at least 2 figures (Lakes Run $190 a carriage-day against Highland's $22; the naive move destroys $1,552,200); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (the 55% marginal load factor is a planning assumption and has to be tested) + external/regulatory (public service obligations on the routes and infrastructure access slots); (4) an urgent next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Маршруты сравнивают по вкладу, а дефицитен подвижной состав: делить надо на вагоно-день.

exhibits.title: MEMO — what drove the margin
exhibits.body_md:
> 1. Volume is stable: 2,400,000 → 2,760,000 t, **+15.00%** over five years, tracking the regional harvest and elevator capacity.
> 2. Margin per tonne is **NOT stable**. 2022–23 covered a drought in a competing export basin: spreads widened and the whole region earned an exceptional carry.
> 3. That basin returned to normal production in 2024. Margin has fallen two years running, and 2025 is close to the 2021 level.
> 4. Elevator capacity is **2,900,000 t**. The headroom for volume growth is nearly exhausted.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you value Thrayven?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the durability of the earnings base raised explicitly; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: first-pass valuation (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What is the seller proposing?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Best year 2023: EBITDA $43,580,000
6.5 × $43,580,000 = $283,270,000
```
**Answer: this is naive #13 — valuing the peak of a cycle as if it were the norm.**

hints.L1: Is the year the seller multiplies the normal year, or the best one?
hints.L2: Look at where in the cycle the chosen year sits before accepting it as the basis for the multiple.

steps.produces: это наив #13 — оценка по пику цикла как по норме

steps.label: Separate the drivers (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: What moved — volume or margin?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Volume: 2,400,000 → 2,760,000 t, +15.00%, a steady climb
Margin: $7.20 → $14.60 → $21.40 → $11.70 → $8.40 — a hump
```
**Answer: the hump is in margin, not in volume. The 2023 peak was a drought in a competing basin, not a structural advantage.**
steps.produces: горб в марже, а не в объёме. Пик 2023 — засуха в конкурирующем бассейне, а не структу

steps.label: CORE: normalisation (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Value it on a normal margin.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Normal years: 2021, 2024, 2025
Margins $7.20 / $11.70 / $8.40 → average $9.10/t

Normalised EBITDA on 2025 volume:
  2,760,000 × $9.10 − $14,600,000 = $10,516,000
Valuation at 6.5×: $68,354,000

NAIVE $283,270,000 · CORRECT $68,354,000 · overstatement 314.42%
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME — the business is worth buying — but the peak figure overstates the value more than fourfold.**
steps.produces: направление ТО ЖЕ — бизнес стоит покупать — но пиковая цифра завышает стоимость в чет

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What would have to be true for the seller's price to hold?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
m* = $21.0797/t (repeating, shown to 4 decimals)
   $9.1000/t →  $68,354,000 → below the ask
  $11.7000/t → $114,998,000 → below the ask
  $21.0797/t → $283,270,000 → tie
  $21.4000/t → $289,016,000 → above the ask
```
**Answer: a margin of $21.0797/t FOREVER — $11.9797 above the normal average, a level reached once in five years at the height of a drought. No volume threshold is printed: even at full capacity of 2,900,000 t the normalised valuation is $76,635,000, still far below the ask.**
steps.produces: нужна маржа $21.0797/т НАВСЕГДА — на $11.9797 выше нормального среднего, уровень, дос

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the investment committee.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — buy, but not at $283,270,000; (2) at least 2 figures ($68,354,000 normalised valuation, overstatement 314.42%); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (elevators are near their ceiling and organic volume growth is exhausted) + external/regulatory (export duties and the weather in a competing basin, neither within the buyer's control); (4) an urgent next step.

cases.difficulty_test: Мультипл применяют к лучшему году цикла, как будто он нормальный.

cases.prompt_md: **Ohmvara Energy** is considering a $34,000,000 network reinforcement programme. Engineering promises to remove 18 MW of losses. Does the programme pass the 8-year payback test?

exhibits.title: BRIDGE — losses in the peak hour

| Component | MW | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| Intake from transmission | 2,400 | 2,400 |
| Transformer losses | −31 | 2,369 |
| Line losses | −64 | 2,305 |
| Substation losses | −18 | 2,287 |
| **Delivered to customers** | | **2,287** |

*Losses in the peak hour: 113 MW of 2,400 MW (4.71%).*

exhibits.title: Load duration curve
triggers: ask how long the network sits at peak
exhibits.body_md:
| Load band | Load MW | Hours/year | Loss factor | MW saved | MWh saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Peak | 2,400 | 400 | 1.0000 | 18.0000 | 7,200 |
| High | 1,800 | 1,800 | 0.5625 | 10.1250 | 18,225 |
| Medium | 1,200 | 3,400 | 0.2500 | 4.5000 | 15,300 |
| Low | 600 | 3,160 | 0.0625 | 1.1250 | 3,555 |
